89:3.en: And the Even and the Odd

89:4.en: And the night when it departeth

89:5.ar: هَلۡ فِي ذَٰلِكَ قَسَمࣱ لِّذِي حِجۡرٍ
89:5.en: There surely is an oath for thinking man

89:6.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ كَيۡفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ
89:6.en: Dost thou not consider how thy Lord dealt with (the tribe of) A'ad

89:8.ar: ٱلَّتِي لَمۡ يُخۡلَقۡ مِثۡلُهَا فِي ٱلۡبِلَٰدِ
89:8.en: The like of which was not created in the lands

89:9.en: And with (the tribe of) Thamud, who clove the rocks in the valley

89:10.en: And with Pharaoh, firm of might

89:11.en: Who (all) were rebellious (to Allah) in these lands

89:13.en: Therefore thy Lord poured on them the disaster of His punishment

89:14.en: Lo! thy Lord is ever watchful

89:15.ar: فَأَمَّا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَأَكۡرَمَهُۥ وَنَعَّمَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَكۡرَمَنِ
89:15.en: As for man, whenever his Lord trieth him by honouring him, and is gracious unto him, he saith: My Lord honoureth me

89:16.ar: وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيۡهِ رِزۡقَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَهَٰنَنِ
89:16.en: But whenever He trieth him by straitening his means of life, he saith: My Lord despiseth me

89:17.en: Nay, but ye (for your part) honour not the orphan

89:18.en: And urge not on the feeding of the poor

89:19.ar: وَتَأۡكُلُونَ ٱلتُّرَاثَ أَكۡلࣰ ا لَّمࣰّ ا
89:19.en: And ye devour heritages with devouring greed

89:20.ar: وَتُحِبُّونَ ٱلۡمَالَ حُبࣰّ ا جَمࣰّ ا
89:20.en: And love wealth with abounding love

89:21.ar: كَلَّآۖ إِذَا دُكَّتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ دَكࣰّ ا دَكࣰّ ا
89:21.en: Nay, but when the earth is ground to atoms, grinding, grinding

89:22.ar: وَجَآءَ رَبُّكَ وَٱلۡمَلَكُ صَفࣰّ ا صَفࣰّ ا
89:22.en: And thy Lord shall come with angels, rank on rank

89:23.ar: وَجِاْيٓءَ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بِجَهَنَّمَۚ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكۡرَىٰ
89:23.en: And hell is brought near that day; on that day man will remember, but how will the remembrance (then avail him)

89:24.en: He will say: Ah, would that I had sent before me (some provision) for my life

89:25.en: None punisheth as He will punish on that day

89:26.en: None bindeth as He then will bind

89:27.en: But ah! thou soul at peace

89:28.en: Return unto thy Lord, content in His good pleasure

IaQr_Nu9CRA.speaker: adnan
IaQr_Nu9CRA.speaker_note: presents his own categorization of Juz Amma, which he says he worked on through his university thesis
IaQr_Nu9CRA.title: Surah Summaries: Al-Fajr
IaQr_Nu9CRA.one_line: Al-Fajr gives the believer a correct perspective on life: ease and hardship are both tests, never signs of Allah's love or contempt.
IaQr_Nu9CRA.summary: He places Al-Fajr in his grouping of Juz Amma as the fourth of the tools that only faith provides: a proper perspective for explaining what happens to us. The surah opens with oaths by opposites, dawn and long nights, even and odd, night passing into day, because life is a series of opposites. It then recalls Aad, Thamud and Pharaoh, who were given everyone's dream of power and wealth and still destroyed, raising the question of whether those gifts were good for them. The core is two verses: the person given plenty says his Lord honoured him, the person whose provision is tightened says his Lord humiliated him, and both are wrong. The shared word is that Allah tested each of them. Nothing personal is implied, and nothing arrives labelled good or bad; we attach the labels by what we do with it. He carefully separates what is simply dealt to us from the consequences of our own choices, which we must own. The surah then names the real problem: not honouring orphans, not feeding the poor, and devouring wealth with endless greed, when sharing our surplus of money, time and attention would solve much of the world's need. Everything is crushed on the Last Day, and the soul at peace, which understood life as tests, is invited into Paradise.

outline.heading: His categorization of the Quran's surahs
outline.gist: He explains that the grouping he uses is his own long work; scholars had other takes and listeners may disagree with the divisions.

outline.heading: The groups of Juz Amma: fundamentals, choices, tools of faith
outline.gist: After the fundamentals and the surahs on choice comes a group giving tools that only faith can generate; lose the faith and you lose the tools.

outline.heading: The fourth tool: a proper perspective on the world
outline.gist: A believer needs a correct way of explaining events to himself and others, a tool not to be taken lightly.

outline.heading: Oaths by opposites: dawn, ten nights, even and odd, the passing night
outline.gist: Allah swears by opposites and by one opposite turning into another, which points to the surah's theme.

outline.heading: Aad, Iram and Thamud: unmatched strength
outline.gist: No nation was like them in their region; 'did you not see' can mean trusted knowledge, which equals seeing. Thamud carved rock in the valleys.

outline.heading: Pharaoh of the stakes and the corruption of all three
outline.gist: The stakes are likely the pyramids, possibly the banners of a great army; all three nations multiplied corruption and were struck with punishment.

outline.heading: Why the stories: were their gifts good or bad for them?
outline.gist: They had everyone's dream of wealth, power and status, yet were destroyed; whether it was good depended on what they did with it.

outline.heading: The honoured man: 'my Lord has honoured me'
outline.gist: Given wealth and pleasure, a person concludes God must love him and that his choices were right.

outline.heading: The restricted man: 'my Lord has humiliated me'
outline.gist: Someone always barely making ends meet concludes God despises him; both conclusions are wrong.

outline.heading: Life swings between opposites
outline.gist: Our hearts move like a barometer between getting and not getting what we want, which is why the surah opened with opposites.

outline.heading: The shared word: Allah tested him
outline.gist: Both verses say Allah tested the person; ease or hardship carries no message about your worth.

outline.heading: What is dealt to you versus what you caused
outline.gist: The verses concern what you had no hand in; a speeding driver on his phone or a heavy smoker must own the consequences, unlike the careful driver or the non-smoking runner with cancer.

outline.heading: Good and bad are understood the same way
outline.gist: Both are tests: ease calls for gratitude and helping others, hardship for perseverance.

outline.heading: The tyrants were given everything and failed; this tool brings calm
outline.gist: Their power did not mean they were loved; whoever holds this understanding lives a calm life, and every Muslim should be taught it.

outline.heading: The believer's affair is always good
outline.gist: The Prophet described the believer who thanks Allah in good times and perseveres in bad, turning both into good.

outline.heading: Nothing comes from the heavens labelled
outline.gist: Ease and difficulty arrive unlabelled; we stamp them good or evil, and what we most wanted can become the worst thing that happened to us.

outline.heading: The real problem: the orphan and the poor
outline.gist: The issue is how we live: not honouring the orphan, who is socially in need, nor urging the feeding of the poor, who are financially in need.

outline.heading: Give your surplus: money, skills, time, a listening ear
outline.gist: If everyone shared what is extra, most problems would fade; often people need attention or someone to talk to more than money, and Ramadan is the time for zakat.

outline.heading: Devouring wealth with endless greed
outline.gist: Consuming inheritance greedily and loving wealth intensely is the problem; there is enough for everyone's needs but not for everyone's greed.

outline.heading: The earth pounded flat; the Lord comes with angels in rows
outline.gist: Everything we own disappears and none of it, not even titles, goes with us; then Allah comes in His glory with the angels.

outline.heading: How simple life really was
outline.gist: Life was just tests to meet with gratitude or perseverance; being alive is already evidence of Allah's love.

outline.heading: 'I wish I had prepared for my life'
outline.gist: On that day people realize the Hereafter is the real, permanent life shaped by their choices, and no one punishes or binds as Allah does.

outline.heading: The soul at peace returns well-pleased and well-pleasing
outline.gist: The one who understood life stayed calm through good and bad, and is invited to join Allah's servants and enter His Paradise.

themes.label: Methodology: how to read texts, tafsir method, intellectual approach
themes.note: His thematic grouping of Juz Amma into fundamentals, choices and tools of faith.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Ease and hardship are both tests with nothing personal in them; only our response gives them meaning.

themes.label: Agency, responsibility and rejecting victim mentality
themes.note: Distinguish what is dealt to you from consequences you caused and must own and repent for.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Ease calls for gratitude and hardship for perseverance; the believer turns both into good.

themes.label: Contentment and acceptance (ridha)
themes.note: This perspective is what gives a calm, settled life.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Share surplus money, skills and time with the socially and financially needy.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Greed and love of possessions, not scarcity, cause most of the world's need.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Everything is crushed, the real life begins, and the tranquil soul is welcomed into Paradise.

hadith.gist: Amazing is the affair of the believer: when good comes he is grateful and when harm comes he perseveres, and both are good for him

maxims: Nothing comes from the heavens labelled
It's not personal; it's just your test
We label what we're given
Enough for our needs, not enough for our greed
You are alive: that is evidence He loves you

stories.point: They had the greatest power and wealth, which did not mean Allah loved them; they failed their test
The careless driver bears the consequence of his choices; the careful one has simply been tested

stories.who: A non-smoking marathon runner with lung cancer
stories.point: Contrasted with a heavy smoker: one illness is a test, the other a consequence to own

takeaways: Do not read your wealth or poverty as a verdict on how Allah sees you
Meet ease with gratitude and giving, and hardship with perseverance
Own the consequences of your own mistakes instead of calling them tests
Share your surplus of money, time, skills and attention with those in need
Keep the Hereafter in view as the real life your choices are shaping

38:2.ar: بَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فِي عِزَّةࣲ وَشِقَاقࣲ‏
38:2.en: Nay, but those who disbelieve are in false pride and schism

38:3.ar: كَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّن قَرۡنࣲ فَنَادَواْ وَّلَاتَ حِينَ مَنَاصࣲ‏
38:3.en: How many a generation We destroyed before them, and they cried out when it was no longer the time for escape

38:4.ar: وَعَجِبُوٓاْ أَن جَآءَهُم مُّنذِرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡۖ وَقَالَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا سَٰحِرࣱ كَذَّابٌ
38:4.en: And they marvel that a warner from among themselves hath come unto them, and the disbelievers say: This is a wizard, a charlatan

38:5.ar: أَجَعَلَ ٱلۡأٓلِهَةَ إِلَٰهࣰ ا وَٰحِدًاۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَيۡءٌ عُجَابࣱ‏
38:5.en: Maketh he the gods One Allah? Lo! that is an astounding thing

38:6.ar: وَٱنطَلَقَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ مِنۡهُمۡ أَنِ ٱمۡشُواْ وَٱصۡبِرُواْ عَلَىٰٓ ءَالِهَتِكُمۡۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَيۡءࣱ يُرَادُ
38:6.en: The chiefs among them go about, exhorting: Go and be staunch to your gods! Lo! this is a thing designed

38:7.ar: مَا سَمِعۡنَا بِهَٰذَا فِي ٱلۡمِلَّةِ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِنۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا ٱخۡتِلَٰقٌ
38:7.en: We have not heard of this in later religion. This is naught but an invention

38:8.ar: أَءُنزِلَ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلذِّكۡرُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِنَاۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ فِي شَكࣲّ مِّن ذِكۡرِيۚ بَل لَّمَّا يَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِ
38:8.en: Hath the reminder been unto him (alone) among us? Nay, but they are in doubt concerning My reminder; nay but they have not yet tasted My doom

38:9.ar: أَمۡ عِندَهُمۡ خَزَآئِنُ رَحۡمَةِ رَبِّكَ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡوَهَّابِ
38:9.en: Or are theirs the treasures of the mercy of thy Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower

38:10.ar: أَمۡ لَهُم مُّلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَاۖ فَلۡيَرۡتَقُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَسۡبَٰبِ
38:10.en: Or is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them theirs? Then let them ascend by ropes

38:11.ar: جُندࣱ مَّا هُنَالِكَ مَهۡزُومࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابِ
38:11.en: A defeated host are (all) the factions that are there

38:12.ar: كَذَّبَتۡ قَبۡلَهُمۡ قَوۡمُ نُوحࣲ وَعَادࣱ وَفِرۡعَوۡنُ ذُو ٱلۡأَوۡتَادِ
38:12.en: The folk of Noah before them denied (their messenger) and (so did the tribe of) A'ad, and Pharaoh firmly planted

38:13.ar: وَثَمُودُ وَقَوۡمُ لُوطࣲ وَأَصۡحَٰبُ لۡـَٔيۡكَةِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابُ
38:13.en: And (the tribe of) Thamud, and the folk of Lot, and the dwellers in the wood: these were the factions

38:14.ar: إِن كُلٌّ إِلَّا كَذَّبَ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ عِقَابِ
38:14.en: Not one of them but did deny the messengers, therefor My doom was justified

38:15.ar: وَمَا يَنظُرُ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِلَّا صَيۡحَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ مَّا لَهَا مِن فَوَاقࣲ‏
38:15.en: These wait for but one Shout, there will be no second thereto

38:16.ar: وَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَا عَجِّل لَّنَا قِطَّنَا قَبۡلَ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
38:16.en: They say: Our Lord! Hasten on for us our fate before the Day of Reckoning

38:17.ar: ٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱذۡكُرۡ عَبۡدَنَا دَاوُۥدَ ذَا ٱلۡأَيۡدِۖ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ
38:17.en: Bear with what they say, and remember Our bondman David, lord of might, Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (toward Allah)

38:18.ar: إِنَّا سَخَّرۡنَا ٱلۡجِبَالَ مَعَهُۥ يُسَبِّحۡنَ بِٱلۡعَشِيِّ وَٱلۡإِشۡرَاقِ
38:18.en: Lo! We subdued the hills to hymn the praises (of their Lord) with him at nightfall and sunrise

38:19.en: And the birds assembled; all were turning unto Him

38:20.ar: وَشَدَدۡنَا مُلۡكَهُۥ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَفَصۡلَ ٱلۡخِطَابِ
38:20.en: We made his kingdom strong and gave him wisdom and decisive speech

38:21.ar: ۞وَهَلۡ أَتَىٰكَ نَبَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَصۡمِ إِذۡ تَسَوَّرُواْ ٱلۡمِحۡرَابَ
38:21.en: And hath the story of the litigants come unto thee? How they climbed the wall into the royal chamber

38:22.ar: إِذۡ دَخَلُواْ عَلَىٰ دَاوُۥدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنۡهُمۡۖ قَالُواْ لَا تَخَفۡۖ خَصۡمَانِ بَغَىٰ بَعۡضُنَا عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تُشۡطِطۡ وَٱهۡدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ
38:22.en: How they burst in upon David, and he was afraid of them. They said: Be not afraid! (We are) two litigants, one of whom hath wronged the other, therefor judge aright between us; be not unjust; and show us the fair way

38:23.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَآ أَخِي لَهُۥ تِسۡعࣱ وَتِسۡعُونَ نَعۡجَةࣰ وَلِيَ نَعۡجَةࣱ وَٰحِدَةࣱ فَقَالَ أَكۡفِلۡنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِي فِي ٱلۡخِطَابِ
38:23.en: Lo! this my brother hath ninety and nine ewes while I had one ewe; and he said: Entrust it to me, and he conquered me in speech

38:24.ar: قَالَ لَقَدۡ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعۡجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِۦۖ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبۡغِي بَعۡضُهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَقَلِيلࣱ مَّا هُمۡۗ وَظَنَّ دَاوُۥدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّٰهُ فَٱسۡتَغۡفَرَ رَبَّهُۥ وَخَرَّۤ رَاكِعࣰ اۤ وَأَنَابَ۩
38:24.en: (David) said: He hath wronged thee in demanding thine ewe in addition to his ewes, and lo! many partners oppress one another, save such as believe and do good works, and they are few. And David guessed that We had tried him, and he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and he bowed himself and fell down prostrate and repented

38:25.ar: فَغَفَرۡنَا لَهُۥ ذَٰلِكَۖ وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلۡفَىٰ وَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
38:25.en: So We forgave him that; and lo! he had access to Our presence and a happy journey's end

38:26.ar: يَٰدَاوُۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَٰكَ خَلِيفَةࣰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ ٱلۡهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدُۢ بِمَا نَسُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
38:26.en: (And it was said unto him): O David! Lo! We have set thee as a viceroy in the earth; therefor judge aright between mankind, and follow not desire that it beguile thee from the way of Allah. Lo! those who wander from the way of Allah have an awful doom, forasmuch as they forgot the Day of Reckoning

38:27.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا بَٰطِلࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ ظَنُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۚ فَوَيۡلࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
38:27.en: And We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them in vain. That is the opinion of those who disbelieve. And woe unto those who disbelieve, from the Fire

38:28.ar: أَمۡ نَجۡعَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ كَٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَمۡ نَجۡعَلُ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ كَٱلۡفُجَّارِ
38:28.en: Shall We treat those who believe and do good works as those who spread corruption in the earth; or shall We treat the pious as the wicked

38:29.ar: كِتَٰبٌ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ إِلَيۡكَ مُبَٰرَكࣱ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوٓاْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
38:29.en: (This is) a Scripture that We have revealed unto thee, full of blessing, that they may ponder its revelations, and that men of understanding may reflect

38:30.ar: وَوَهَبۡنَا لِدَاوُۥدَ سُلَيۡمَٰنَۚ نِعۡمَ ٱلۡعَبۡدُ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ
38:30.en: And We bestowed on David, Solomon. How excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (toward Allah)

38:31.ar: إِذۡ عُرِضَ عَلَيۡهِ بِٱلۡعَشِيِّ ٱلصَّٰفِنَٰتُ ٱلۡجِيَادُ
38:31.en: When there were shown to him at eventide lightfooted coursers

38:32.ar: فَقَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَحۡبَبۡتُ حُبَّ ٱلۡخَيۡرِ عَن ذِكۡرِ رَبِّي حَتَّىٰ تَوَارَتۡ بِٱلۡحِجَابِ
38:32.en: And he said: Lo! I have preferred the good things (of the world) to the remembrance of my Lord; till they were taken out of sight behind the curtain

38:33.ar: رُدُّوهَا عَلَيَّۖ فَطَفِقَ مَسۡحَۢا بِٱلسُّوقِ وَٱلۡأَعۡنَاقِ
38:33.en: (Then he said): Bring them back to me, and fell to slashing (with his sword their) legs and necks

38:34.ar: وَلَقَدۡ فَتَنَّا سُلَيۡمَٰنَ وَأَلۡقَيۡنَا عَلَىٰ كُرۡسِيِّهِۦ جَسَدࣰ ا ثُمَّ أَنَابَ
38:34.en: And verily We tried Solomon, and set upon his throne a (mere) body. Then did he repent

38:35.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغۡفِرۡ لِي وَهَبۡ لِي مُلۡكࣰ ا لَّا يَنۢبَغِي لِأَحَدࣲ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِيٓۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡوَهَّابُ
38:35.en: He said: My Lord! Forgive me and bestow on me sovereignty such as shall not belong to any after me. Lo! Thou art the Bestower

38:36.ar: فَسَخَّرۡنَا لَهُ ٱلرِّيحَ تَجۡرِي بِأَمۡرِهِۦ رُخَآءً حَيۡثُ أَصَابَ
38:36.en: So We made the wind subservient unto him, setting fair by his command whithersoever he intended

38:37.en: And the unruly, every builder and diver (made We subservient)

38:38.en: And others linked together in chains

38:39.ar: هَٰذَا عَطَآؤُنَا فَٱمۡنُنۡ أَوۡ أَمۡسِكۡ بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابࣲ‏
38:39.en: (Saying): This is Our gift, so bestow thou, or withhold, without reckoning

38:40.ar: وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلۡفَىٰ وَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
38:40.en: And lo! he hath favour with Us, and a happy journey's end

38:41.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ عَبۡدَنَآ أَيُّوبَ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ بِنُصۡبࣲ وَعَذَابٍ
38:41.en: And make mention (O Muhammad) of Our bondman Job, when he cried unto his Lord (saying): Lo! the devil doth afflict me with distress and torment

38:42.ar: ٱرۡكُضۡ بِرِجۡلِكَۖ هَٰذَا مُغۡتَسَلُۢ بَارِدࣱ وَشَرَابࣱ‏
38:42.en: (And it was said unto him): Strike the ground with thy foot. This (spring) is a cool bath and a refreshing drink

38:43.ar: وَوَهَبۡنَا لَهُۥٓ أَهۡلَهُۥ وَمِثۡلَهُم مَّعَهُمۡ رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنَّا وَذِكۡرَىٰ لِأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
38:43.en: And We bestowed on him (again) his household and therewith the like thereof, a mercy from Us, and a memorial for men of understanding

38:44.ar: وَخُذۡ بِيَدِكَ ضِغۡثࣰ ا فَٱضۡرِب بِّهِۦ وَلَا تَحۡنَثۡۗ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَٰهُ صَابِرࣰ اۚ نِّعۡمَ ٱلۡعَبۡدُ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابࣱ‏
38:44.en: And (it was said unto him): Take in thine hand a branch and smite therewith, and break not thine oath. Lo! We found him steadfast, how excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (to his Lord)

38:45.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ عِبَٰدَنَآ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ أُوْلِي ٱلۡأَيۡدِي وَٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ
38:45.en: And make mention of Our bondmen, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, men of parts and vision

38:46.en: Lo! We purified them with a pure thought, remembrance of the Home (of the Hereafter)

38:47.en: Lo! in Our sight they are verily of the elect, the excellent

38:48.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ إِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَٱلۡيَسَعَ وَذَا ٱلۡكِفۡلِۖ وَكُلࣱّ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَخۡيَارِ
38:48.en: And make mention of Ishmael and Elisha and Dhu'l-Kifl. All are of the chosen

38:49.ar: هَٰذَا ذِكۡرࣱۚ وَإِنَّ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
38:49.en: This is a reminder. And lo! for those who ward off (evil) is a happy journey's end

38:50.en: Gardens of Eden, whereof the gates are opened for them

38:51.ar: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ فِيهَا يَدۡعُونَ فِيهَا بِفَٰكِهَةࣲ كَثِيرَةࣲ وَشَرَابࣲ‏
38:51.en: Wherein, reclining, they call for plenteous fruit and cool drink (that is) therein

38:52.en: And with them are those of modest gaze, companions

38:53.en: This it is that ye are promised for the Day of Reckoning

38:54.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَرِزۡقُنَا مَا لَهُۥ مِن نَّفَادٍ
38:54.en: Lo! this in truth is Our provision, which will never waste away

38:55.en: This (is for the righteous). And lo! for the transgressors there with be an evil journey's end

38:56.en: Hell, where they will burn, an evil resting-place

38:57.en: Here is a boiling and an ice-cold draught, so let them taste it

38:58.en: And other (torment) of the kind in pairs (the two extremes)

38:59.ar: هَٰذَا فَوۡجࣱ مُّقۡتَحِمࣱ مَّعَكُمۡ لَا مَرۡحَبَۢا بِهِمۡۚ إِنَّهُمۡ صَالُواْ ٱلنَّارِ
38:59.en: Here is an army rushing blindly with you. (Those who are already in the Fire say): No word of welcome for them. Lo! they will roast at the Fire

38:60.ar: قَالُواْ بَلۡ أَنتُمۡ لَا مَرۡحَبَۢا بِكُمۡۖ أَنتُمۡ قَدَّمۡتُمُوهُ لَنَاۖ فَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡقَرَارُ
38:60.en: They say: Nay, but you (misleaders), for you there is no word of welcome. Ye prepared this for us (by your misleading). Now hapless is the plight

38:61.ar: قَالُواْ رَبَّنَا مَن قَدَّمَ لَنَا هَٰذَا فَزِدۡهُ عَذَابࣰ ا ضِعۡفࣰ ا فِي ٱلنَّارِ
38:61.en: They say: Our Lord! Whoever did prepare this for us, oh, give him double portion of the Fire

38:62.ar: وَقَالُواْ مَا لَنَا لَا نَرَىٰ رِجَالࣰ ا كُنَّا نَعُدُّهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَشۡرَارِ
38:62.en: And they say: What aileth us that we behold not men whom we were wont to count among the wicked

38:63.ar: أَتَّخَذۡنَٰهُمۡ سِخۡرِيًّا أَمۡ زَاغَتۡ عَنۡهُمُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ
38:63.en: Did we take them (wrongly) for a laughing-stock, or have our eyes missed them

38:64.ar: إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَحَقࣱّ تَخَاصُمُ أَهۡلِ ٱلنَّارِ
38:64.en: Lo! that is very truth: the wrangling of the dwellers in the Fire

38:71.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي خَٰلِقُۢ بَشَرࣰ ا مِّن طِينࣲ‏
38:71.en: When thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to create a mortal out of mire

38:72.ar: فَإِذَا سَوَّيۡتُهُۥ وَنَفَخۡتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي فَقَعُواْ لَهُۥ سَٰجِدِينَ
38:72.en: And when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My Spirit, then fall down before him prostrate

38:73.en: The angels fell down prostrate, every one

38:74.ar: إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
38:74.en: Saving Iblis; he was scornful and became one of the disbelievers

38:75.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓإِبۡلِيسُ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَن تَسۡجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقۡتُ بِيَدَيَّۖ أَسۡتَكۡبَرۡتَ أَمۡ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلۡعَالِينَ
38:75.en: He said: O Iblis! What hindereth thee from falling prostrate before that which I have created with both My hands? Art thou too proud or art thou of the high exalted

38:76.ar: قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡهُ خَلَقۡتَنِي مِن نَّارࣲ وَخَلَقۡتَهُۥ مِن طِينࣲ‏
38:76.en: He said: I am better than him. Thou createdst me of fire, whilst him Thou didst create of clay

38:77.en: He said: Go forth from hence, for lo! thou art outcast

38:78.ar: وَإِنَّ عَلَيۡكَ لَعۡنَتِيٓ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلدِّينِ
38:78.en: And lo! My curse is on thee till the Day of Judgment

38:79.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ فَأَنظِرۡنِيٓ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ يُبۡعَثُونَ
38:79.en: He said: My Lord! Reprieve me till the day when they are raised

38:80.en: He said: Lo! thou art of those reprieved

38:81.en: Until the day of the time appointed

38:82.en: He said: Then, by Thy might, I surely will beguile them every one

38:83.en: Save Thy single-minded slaves among them

38:84.en: He said: The Truth is, and the Truth I speak

38:85.ar: لَأَمۡلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ وَمِمَّن تَبِعَكَ مِنۡهُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
38:85.en: That I shall fill hell with thee and with such of them as follow thee, together

38:86.ar: قُلۡ مَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ أَجۡرࣲ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلۡمُتَكَلِّفِينَ
38:86.en: Say (O Muhammad, unto mankind): I ask of you no fee for this, and I am no simulating

38:87.en: Lo! it is naught else than a reminder for all peoples

38:88.en: And ye will come in time to know the truth thereof

159GS6n3mj4.speaker: adnan
159GS6n3mj4.speaker_note: Surah Summaries series at MWN, his usual cluster framing and voice throughout
159GS6n3mj4.title: Surat Sad Summary
159GS6n3mj4.one_line: Surah Sad as a lesson in acknowledging mistakes and returning to the truth, through Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub and the refusal of Iblis.
159GS6n3mj4.summary: He places Surah Sad in a cluster of surahs about submission to Allah and reads it as a surah about one trait: admitting a mistake and returning to what is right without shame. The opening verses diagnose disbelief not as disagreement but as pride and stubborn clinging to error, shown in the Quraysh leaders who reject the message simply because it is new, as earlier nations did. He then walks through the prophets in the surah. Dawud, a king, judge and prophet, rules after hearing only one litigant, and although he could have blamed the intruders who climbed into his private place of worship, he immediately seeks forgiveness; the lesson is that anyone who judges must hear the other side, and this is where the word khalifah enters the human job description. Sulayman admits that love of his horses delayed his prayer, and he rejects the story that he slaughtered them. Ayyub, after years of patience, is corrected for an oath against his wife. Each looks at his own fault, not at others'. The people of Hell wonder why certain sinners are missing: they returned to Allah at some point. Iblis is the counterexample who knew he was wrong and stayed. He asks listeners to make returning to the truth part of who they are.

outline.heading: Surah Sad: returning to the truth even against yourself
outline.gist: The surah's message is submission through acknowledging mistakes and going back to righteousness without embarrassment, a trait of both Muslims and good human beings.

outline.heading: Bal: the real cause of disbelief is pride and stubbornness
outline.gist: The particle bal signals that the stated reasons are not the real ones; the disbelievers are held back by self-importance and by insisting on staying in what they know is wrong.

outline.heading: Rejecting the message because it is new
outline.gist: The Quraysh leaders tell people to hold to their idols because nobody before ever said this; refusing something only because it is unfamiliar is part of the disease.

outline.heading: Earlier nations who refused their prophets the same way
outline.gist: The surah lists the people of Nuh, Lut, Shuayb and the confederates, who saw they were wrong yet refused, and warns Quraysh that the same outcome awaits.

outline.heading: Interlude
Dawud's many roles and the two intruders
outline.gist: Dawud was king, commander, prophet, artist and judge, and kept private time for worship; two disputants climb his wall and bring him the case of the 99 ewes and the one.

outline.heading: Judging after hearing one side
outline.gist: Dawud rules for the complainant without hearing the other man; whoever judges or takes a side is obliged to hear the other party however weak its case looks. He realizes, repents and is forgiven.

outline.heading: The khalifah: judging with truth, not desire
outline.gist: Allah names Dawud a khalifah and tells him to judge by truth and not follow desire; the word first appears in a surah about admitting error, a fitting place.

outline.heading: Creation has a purpose, so cling to the truth
outline.gist: The heavens and earth were not made in vain as the disbelievers think; those who return to the right are not equal to those who do not.

outline.heading: Dawud had every excuse and used none
outline.gist: It was his day off, they invaded his privacy and they were angels testing him, yet he did not rationalize or punish them; he simply admitted his mistake, the mark of those close to Allah.

outline.heading: Sulayman's horses and the delayed prayer
outline.gist: Sulayman's love of fine horses delayed his prayer until sunset; he admits it openly.

outline.heading: Rejecting the claim that he slaughtered the horses
outline.gist: The verb means stroking the horses, not killing them; the slaughter story comes from Israelite reports that contradict the mercy of prophets and the point of the passage.

outline.heading: Forgetting inshallah and the trial of the child
outline.gist: Sulayman vowed to father sons who would all serve Allah without saying inshallah, then had one child born disabled, and again openly asked forgiveness.

outline.heading: Sulayman's dua for a unique kingdom
outline.gist: Kings who admit their mistakes can be trusted with power; he asks for a dominion like no other to show that strength can serve Allah, and it is granted.

outline.heading: Focus on your own mistakes, not other people's
outline.gist: The prophets in the surah all had power or hardship to blame, but they looked only at their own fault, because each person answers for his own actions.

outline.heading: Ayyub's oath against his wife
outline.gist: After years of illness and loss, Ayyub swears in anger to strike his wife for her complaint; once healed he is told to fulfill it with a handful of grass, a correction even for the most patient.

outline.heading: Awwab: the one who keeps returning
outline.gist: Allah praises Ayyub as an excellent servant who constantly returns; the quality the surah celebrates is returning, not never erring.

outline.heading: The people of Hell ask where the 'evil' people went
outline.gist: Those in Hell wonder why men they mocked as wrongdoers are missing; the answer is that those people at some point admitted their wrong and returned to Allah.

outline.heading: Iblis: the one who knew and did not return
outline.gist: Allah asks Iblis whether he is arrogant or truly higher; either way he could have admitted the mistake, but he insisted fire is better than clay and stayed with his error.

outline.heading: The Prophet claims no perfection, only return
outline.gist: The surah closes with the Prophet saying he asks no reward and pretends to be nothing he is not; the surah is a reminder whose importance people will learn later.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Returning to the right after a mistake, openly and without shame, is the trait the whole surah teaches through each prophet.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Disbelief is driven by pride and stubbornly staying in error, not by honest disagreement.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Iblis is the model of arrogance that refuses to retract a known mistake.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Anyone who judges or takes sides must hear the other party, however obvious one side seems.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Dawud refused to rationalize his mistake despite every excuse being available.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Focus on your own faults rather than others', since you answer only for yourself.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Dawud, Sulayman and Ayyub each acknowledge a mistake openly.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: The khalifah role is defined by judging with truth and not desire; leaders who admit error can be trusted with power.

themes.label: Methodology: how to read texts, tafsir method, intellectual approach
themes.note: He rejects Israelite reports that make Sulayman slaughter innocent horses as contrary to the character of prophets.

hadith.gist: Sulayman said he would father many sons who would all strive for Allah but did not say inshallah, and only one child was born, incomplete

maxims: Accept the truth even if it is against yourself
If you judge, you must hear the other side
Focus on what you are doing wrong, not others

stories.point: He judged after hearing one side, then admitted it at once despite every excuse.
He openly admitted that love of his horses delayed his prayer.
Even a small omission is acknowledged and repented.
Even after great patience he was corrected for mistreating his wife and given a way to make it right.
Knowing you are wrong and staying there is the most dangerous state.

takeaways: Admit mistakes openly when they are pointed out, without embarrassment
Do not rationalize your errors even when you have good excuses
Hear both sides before judging or taking a side in a dispute
Look at your own faults instead of other people's
Do not reject something only because it is new to you

88:1.en: Hath there come unto thee tidings of the Overwhelming

88:2.en: On that day (many) faces will be downcast

88:6.ar: لَّيۡسَ لَهُمۡ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِن ضَرِيعࣲ‏
88:6.en: No food for them save bitter thorn-fruit

88:7.ar: لَّا يُسۡمِنُ وَلَا يُغۡنِي مِن جُوعࣲ‏
88:7.en: Which doth not nourish nor release from hunger

88:8.en: In that day other faces will be calm

88:11.en: Where they hear no idle speech

88:17.ar: أَفَلَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡإِبِلِ كَيۡفَ خُلِقَتۡ
88:17.en: Will they not regard the camels, how they are created

88:18.en: And the heaven, how it is raised

88:19.en: And the hills, how they are set up

88:20.en: And the earth, how it is spread

88:21.en: Remind them, for thou art but a remembrancer

88:22.en: Thou art not at all a warder over them

88:23.en: But whoso is averse and disbelieveth

88:24.en: Allah will punish him with direst punishment

88:25.en: Lo! unto Us is their return

Bpp18jrjiB8.speaker: adnan
Bpp18jrjiB8.speaker_note: Surah Summaries series at MWN, his cluster framing and voice throughout
Bpp18jrjiB8.title: Surah Al-Ghashiyah Summary
Bpp18jrjiB8.one_line: Revealed at the Prophet's lowest hour, Al-Ghashiyah gives the believer's third tool: relentless striving for Allah until death, since nothing here compares to the Overwhelming Event.
Bpp18jrjiB8.summary: He presents Al-Ghashiyah as the third surah in a cluster about the toolkit faith gives a believer, and its tool is mujahadah: sticking to your mission for Allah no matter how often you fail. Ordinary perseverance lasts until a person gets tired and moves on; faith-based perseverance has no off switch except losing faith, which is what baffled the Prophet's opponents. To show how the surah teaches this he sets its revelation in the year of grief: the boycott of Banu Hashim, the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah, the rejection at Taif and being barred from Makkah, the day the Prophet himself called his worst. At that moment Allah asks whether he has heard of the Overwhelming Event, where faces labour and exhaust themselves in worship that no one records any more, like writing an exam after time is called. Hardship in this life always has some light because deeds are still being recorded. The joyful faces are pleased with their sa'y, the striving they kept up until death even if the goal was never reached. The believer's job is to remind, not to control people or decide their punishment, and to keep going whether or not anyone listens.

outline.heading: The third cluster: the toolkit faith gives you
outline.gist: After surahs on fundamentals and on choices, this group lists tools Islam gives for facing life that upbringing and experience alone cannot.

outline.heading: Al-Ghashiyah's tool: mujahadah
outline.gist: After the first two tools, this surah gives continuing struggle for the sake of Allah, mujahadah or musabarah.

outline.heading: Life's perseverance versus faith's perseverance
outline.gist: Life teaches you to try for a while and then move on; faith tells you that once you know your mission you never stop, whatever happens.

outline.heading: The Prophet had no off button
outline.gist: His opponents could not understand his relentlessness through every kind of abuse; the only thing that stops a believer is losing the faith itself.

outline.heading: Revealed in the year of grief
outline.gist: The surah's depth depends on knowing it came in the tenth year of prophethood, the year of grief.

outline.heading: The boycott of Banu Hashim
outline.gist: For three years his clan was cut off from food, trade, marriage and travel, confined between two hills of Makkah.

outline.heading: Losing Abu Talib and Khadijah
outline.gist: Within a month he lost his protector outside the house and his first believer and supporter inside it.

outline.heading: Rejection at Taif and being barred from Makkah
outline.gist: Seeking support from the nearest power, he was rejected rudely and then denied re-entry to Makkah; one difficulty after another.

outline.heading: His worst day, and the question of the surah
outline.gist: He told Aisha his worst day was not Uhud but walking aimlessly back from Taif; at that hour came: has the tale of the Overwhelming Event reached you?

outline.heading: Al-Ghashiyah: the event with no way out
outline.gist: The word means what smothers and suffocates; feeling low is human, but Allah asks whether what you face now compares with that.

outline.heading: Labouring, weary faces: worship that no one records
outline.gist: On that day people finally work hard at prayer and dua with all their heart, but the book is sealed and no one is listening; that is true distress.

outline.heading: Burning fire, boiling drink, food that does not nourish
outline.gist: After all that effort they are taken to the Fire; compare and ask which is harder.

outline.heading: The joyful faces
outline.gist: All the stress and pain of striving now is for a day of soft, relaxed, joyful faces.

outline.heading: Be humbled in this world, not on that day
outline.gist: Humility before Allah, knowing we can never repay what we were given, belongs in this life; arriving at it on that day is too late.

outline.heading: Here there is always light: your deeds are still recorded
outline.gist: Even a terminal situation in this world holds hope because what you say and do is still written for you.

outline.heading: The exam after time is called
outline.gist: The best answer ever written counts for nothing once time is up; the same holds on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Pleased with their sa'y, not just their deeds
outline.gist: Sa'y is the striving toward a vision of good that one may never complete; you are rewarded for it in full whether or not you saw its fruits.

outline.heading: Memorizing the Quran an ayah a day
outline.gist: If you die still memorizing, it counts as striving toward the whole; if you stop, only what you memorized is counted.

outline.heading: Keep going until you meet Allah; the lofty garden
outline.gist: Striving only counts as sa'y if you die still doing it; its reward is a high garden where no idle word is heard.

outline.heading: Springs, raised couches, cups and carpets
outline.gist: Paradise is pictured as rest and comfort because the person worked hard until death.

outline.heading: What if the Prophet had given up?
outline.gist: After the boycott, the deaths and Taif, he could have said he could not continue; the surah tells him what is truly hard and that the happy ones are those who stuck to it.

outline.heading: Look at the camel, the sky, the mountains, the earth
outline.gist: Creation has been set up so you can live comfortably and do your job.

outline.heading: Your job is to remind
outline.gist: Speak the truth, educate and raise awareness about Allah; that is the job.

outline.heading: You are not a controller over them
outline.gist: Muslims must drop the urge to control people; a teacher offers knowledge and lets people decide, and pushing a personal agenda is corruption.

outline.heading: They are not listening. So what?
outline.gist: Being ignored was never a reason to stop; keep walking the course however heavy it gets, because the Overwhelming Event is heavier.

outline.heading: Dua and sujood into nothingness
outline.gist: On that day their dua is not received and they cannot prostrate, because they were asked to do it in this life.

outline.heading: Leave the punishment to Allah
outline.gist: Those who turn away will be punished by Allah Himself; our task is to remind, teach and be an example, and their return and reckoning are His.

outline.heading: The third tool: grit until you meet Allah
outline.gist: Only believers keep going regardless of changing circumstances; that relentlessness is the tool the surah gives.

themes.label: Mujahadah: striving as a way of life
themes.note: Faith-based perseverance has no stopping point short of losing faith.

themes.label: Mujahadah: striving as a way of life
themes.note: Sa'y is striving kept up until death, rewarded in full even when the goal is never reached.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: The year of grief, the boycott, two deaths and Taif frame the surah's message.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Effort after the record is sealed is worthless; humility and hard work belong in this life.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Any worldly hardship still has light because deeds are recorded, unlike the Overwhelming Event.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: The job is to remind, not to control people or decide their punishment, and to keep going whether or not they listen.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Feel humbled before Allah now, not on the Day of Judgment.

hadith.gist: Aisha asked the Prophet whether any day was worse than Uhud; he said the worst was the day at Taif, when he walked back not knowing where he was going

There is no off button except losing your faith

takeaways: Once you know your mission for Allah, keep at it however often you fail
Set long-term goals of good and keep striving toward them until death
Measure today's hardship against the Overwhelming Event
Remind and teach without trying to control people or judge their fate

61:1.ar: سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
61:1.en: All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifieth Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise

61:2.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
61:2.en: O ye who believe! Why say ye that which ye do not

61:3.ar: كَبُرَ مَقۡتًا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَن تَقُولُواْ مَا لَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
61:3.en: It is most hateful in the sight of Allah that ye say that which ye do not

61:4.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِۦ صَفࣰّ ا كَأَنَّهُم بُنۡيَٰنࣱ مَّرۡصُوصࣱ‏
61:4.en: Lo! Allah loveth them who battle for His cause in ranks, as if they were a solid structure

61:5.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ يَٰقَوۡمِ لِمَ تُؤۡذُونَنِي وَقَد تَّعۡلَمُونَ أَنِّي رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَيۡكُمۡۖ فَلَمَّا زَاغُوٓاْ أَزَاغَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
61:5.en: And (remember) when Moses said unto his people: O my people! Why persecute ye me, when ye well know that I am Allah's messenger unto you? So when they went astray Allah sent their hearts astray. And Allah guideth not the evil-living folk

61:6.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ يَٰبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ إِنِّي رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَيۡكُم مُّصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَمُبَشِّرَۢا بِرَسُولࣲ يَأۡتِي مِنۢ بَعۡدِي ٱسۡمُهُۥٓ أَحۡمَدُۖ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ قَالُواْ هَٰذَا سِحۡرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
61:6.en: And when Jesus son of Mary said: O Children of Israel! Lo! I am the messenger of Allah unto you, confirming that which was (revealed) before me in the Torah, and bringing good tidings of a messenger who cometh after me, whose name is the Praised One. Yet when he hath come unto them with clear proofs, they say: This is mere magic

61:10.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ تِجَٰرَةࣲ تُنجِيكُم مِّنۡ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
61:10.en: O ye who believe! Shall I show you a commerce that will save you from a painful doom

61:11.ar: تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَتُجَٰهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ بِأَمۡوَٰلِكُمۡ وَأَنفُسِكُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
61:11.en: Ye should believe in Allah and His messenger, and should strive for the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if ye did but know

61:12.ar: يَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ ذُنُوبَكُمۡ وَيُدۡخِلۡكُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ وَمَسَٰكِنَ طَيِّبَةࣰ فِي جَنَّٰتِ عَدۡنࣲۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
61:12.en: He will forgive you your sins and bring you into Gardens underneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eden. That is the supreme triumph

61:13.ar: وَأُخۡرَىٰ تُحِبُّونَهَاۖ نَصۡرࣱ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَفَتۡحࣱ قَرِيبࣱۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
61:13.en: And (He will give you) another (blessing) which ye love: help from Allah and present victory. Give good tidings (O Muhammad) to believers

61:14.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُوٓاْ أَنصَارَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَا قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ لِلۡحَوَارِيِّـۧنَ مَنۡ أَنصَارِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ قَالَ ٱلۡحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحۡنُ أَنصَارُ ٱللَّهِۖ فَـَٔامَنَت طَّآئِفَةࣱ مِّنۢ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ وَكَفَرَت طَّآئِفَةࣱۖ فَأَيَّدۡنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ عَلَىٰ عَدُوِّهِمۡ فَأَصۡبَحُواْ ظَٰهِرِينَ
61:14.en: O ye who believe! Be Allah's helpers, even as Jesus son of Mary said unto the disciples: Who are my helpers for Allah? They said: We are Allah's helpers. And a party of the Children of Israel believed, while a party disbelieved. Then We strengthened those who believed against their foe, and they became the uppermost

62:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ لَفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
62:2.en: He it is Who hath sent among the unlettered ones a messenger of their own, to recite unto them His revelations and to make them grow, and to teach them the Scripture and wisdom, though heretofore they were indeed in error manifest

62:5.ar: مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ حُمِّلُواْ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةَ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَحۡمِلُوهَا كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡحِمَارِ يَحۡمِلُ أَسۡفَارَۢاۚ بِئۡسَ مَثَلُ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
62:5.en: The likeness of those who are entrusted with the Law of Moses, yet apply it not, is as the likeness of the ass carrying books. Wretched is the likeness of folk who deny the revelations of Allah. And Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

62:6.ar: قُلۡ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوٓاْ إِن زَعَمۡتُمۡ أَنَّكُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءُ لِلَّهِ مِن دُونِ ٱلنَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُاْ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
62:6.en: Say (O Muhammad): O ye who are Jews! If ye claim that ye are favoured of Allah apart from (all) mankind, then long for death if ye are truthful

62:7.ar: وَلَا يَتَمَنَّوۡنَهُۥٓ أَبَدَۢا بِمَا قَدَّمَتۡ أَيۡدِيهِمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
62:7.en: But they will never long for it because of all that their own hands have sent before, and Allah is Aware of evil-doers

62:8.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ ٱلَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنۡهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ مُلَٰقِيكُمۡۖ ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَٰلِمِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
62:8.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Lo! the death from which ye shrink will surely meet you, and afterward ye will be returned unto the Knower of the Invisible and the Visible, and He will tell you what ye used to do

62:9.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَوٰةِ مِن يَوۡمِ ٱلۡجُمُعَةِ فَٱسۡعَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَذَرُواْ ٱلۡبَيۡعَۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
62:9.en: O ye who believe! When the call is heard for the prayer of the day of congregation, haste unto remembrance of Allah and leave your trading. That is better for you if ye did but know

62:10.ar: فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةُ فَٱنتَشِرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرࣰ ا لَّعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
62:10.en: And when the prayer is ended, then disperse in the land and seek of Allah's bounty, and remember Allah much, that ye may be successful

62:11.ar: وَإِذَا رَأَوۡاْ تِجَٰرَةً أَوۡ لَهۡوًا ٱنفَضُّوٓاْ إِلَيۡهَا وَتَرَكُوكَ قَآئِمࣰ اۚ قُلۡ مَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنَ ٱللَّهۡوِ وَمِنَ ٱلتِّجَٰرَةِۚ وَٱللَّهُ خَيۡرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ
62:11.en: But when they spy some merchandise or pastime they break away to it and leave thee standing. Say: That which Allah hath is better than pastime and than merchandise, and Allah is the Best of providers

AowhDlUVZuc.title: Surat As-Saff and Al-Jumu'ah: Summaries
AowhDlUVZuc.one_line: As-Saff as a contract to put the ummah before yourself; Al-Jumu'ah as Islam's built-in system of leadership that Muslims are wasting.
AowhDlUVZuc.summary: A Sunday lesson summarizing two Medinan surahs of the 28th juz, which he describes as organizing Muslim society. As-Saff, he says, is built around a contract. It opens by rebuking believers who say what they do not do: having joined the ummah, you committed to put its interest before your own. Fighters standing in a row like a solid structure is the Quran's ultimate example of that sacrifice, and the prayer row symbolizes the same unity. Musa's and Isa's peoples failed because self-interest divided them, which is also why they rejected the prophet Isa foretold as Ahmad. The surah's centre is the 'trade' of 61:10-13: give your wealth and yourself, receive forgiveness, Paradise and victory. Its close calls believers to be helpers of Allah as the disciples and the Ansar were. Al-Jumu'ah, he argues, installs a system of leadership in Islam: the khateeb inherits the four tasks of the prophets in 62:2, so khutbahs must be relevant, simple and purposeful. A billion people gathering weekly with so little progress shows how badly the platform is wasted, and Muslims who own a heritage they never read are the donkey carrying books.

outline.heading: The Medinan cluster of the 28th juz
outline.gist: These surahs, all revealed in Madinah, organize Muslim life: relations among Muslims, with non-Muslims near and far, with enemies and traitors, with fellow citizens and spouses, along with leadership and domestic law.

outline.heading: A surah built on a contract
outline.gist: As-Saff revolves around a verse offering a contract: keep the commitment you made on becoming Muslim to hold the group together and serve its message. Organizing a large people calls for a contract.

outline.heading: Why do you say what you do not do?
outline.gist: After the opening glorification comes the axis of the surah: saying what you do not do is hateful to Allah. At the level of society, you joined the ummah and pledged to work for its unity, service and success in every field, so why are you not doing it?

outline.heading: The solid row
outline.gist: Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row like a solid structure. Combat is rarely what is asked, but it is the Quran's ultimate example of putting the ummah's interest before your own; the prayer row is a symbol of the same oneness and care for one another.

outline.heading: Musa's people: self-interest over the nation
outline.gist: Musa asks why his people harm him. He sets aside specific tafsir narrations that lack authenticity for the charge the Quran repeats about 25 times: they divided, became egocentric rather than nation-centred, and when they deviated Allah turned their hearts away.

outline.heading: Isa foretells Ahmad
outline.gist: Isa confirms the Torah and foretells a messenger after him named Ahmad, the only place the Prophet is so named. His people refused him because following him meant giving up something of themselves for the bigger picture.

outline.heading: The trade that saves from a painful punishment
outline.gist: Allah's business proposal: believe, and exhaust your wealth, time and lives in His cause; in return, forgiveness, the highest ranks of Paradise and the thing you love, victory and prosperity. Putting the ummah before your likes, dislikes and happiness is the contract in the Quran: have you signed it?

outline.heading: Be helpers of Allah
outline.gist: Do not just say you believe and pray: be ansar of Allah, those who stand by and strengthen His message, as the people of Madinah were named for standing by the Prophet and as the disciples answered Isa. Those who signed the contract and lived by it prevailed.

outline.heading: Interlude
Leadership comes installed with Islam
outline.gist: Al-Jumu'ah is about leadership: Islam comes with a built-in system you only need to activate. Any few Muslims anywhere, from Alaska to the Amazon, find each other, build a masjid and hold Jumuah, and whoever gives it is the one who leads and decides.

outline.heading: A billion people a week and no progress
outline.gist: Around a billion people gather every week, even virtually during Covid; no other group does this. If those messages had benefit, structure and unity, how could Muslims fail to progress? Muslims must be professionals at ruining things.

outline.heading: The khateeb takes the prophets' role
outline.gist: 62:2 lists the four reasons prophets were sent, and the khateeb inherits them. He should not be handed a paper to read or speak on issues irrelevant to the people in front of him; Jumuah was how the Prophet and the companions led communities, and everything the ummah needs can happen there.

outline.heading: Allah gathers them; offer a message worth hearing
outline.gist: His lessons draw ten to twenty people while his khutbah fills the masjid, not for him but because Allah obliges them to come, so the khateeb is obliged to deliver and will be held to account. Tell people about Allah, help them purify themselves, teach the rulings and the wisdom to practise them, without controversial detail.

outline.heading: The donkey carrying books
outline.gist: Those given the Torah who did not live by it are like a donkey loaded with books. Descending from a heritage that united science and religion, with over 300,000 Islamic books and the Quran for 1,400 years, means nothing if you read and reflect on none of it.

outline.heading: When the Jumuah narrative dies
outline.gist: When Jumuah stops doing its job, people are Muslim only by birth and feel no connection; youth find it more meaningless each week and come only because they must, which cannot last. The leadership system is there for the taking.

outline.heading: Wish for death, then
outline.gist: Being given guidance, being born Muslim or speaking Arabic does not make you Allah's ally. Claim it and wish for death; no one does, because all know how far they are. Death will find you, so use your time well.

outline.heading: Allah does His part: the Friday call
outline.gist: With one verse Allah gathers a billion people every week, by a generous estimate; with that much in common, failing to progress is baffling.

outline.heading: Leave trade, then seek His bounty
outline.gist: At the call, leave buying and selling; after the prayer, go out and work, seeking Allah's bounty and remembering Him throughout, carrying the message you heard.

outline.heading: The caravan that left him standing
outline.gist: Early on, when a trade caravan arrived during the khutbah, people left the Prophet standing; it took time to teach that Jumuah outranks livelihood and distraction, since Allah provides. Keep your priorities straight and listen to your leader.

outline.heading: Jumuah left a skeleton
outline.gist: Leadership and proper narratives have been taken out of Jumuah, leaving a skeleton of what it was; it can return. Allah gathers people not for His sake but for their benefit: this is how a society is built and strengthened.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Unity of Muslims: from shared similarities to a united stand
themes.note: As-Saff asks believers to stand like a solid structure and keep the ummah united, with the nation's interest ahead of personal likes and dislikes.

themes.label: Oaths, promises, trust and loyalty
themes.note: Saying what you do not do breaks the commitment made on becoming Muslim; the surah frames that commitment as a contract.

themes.label: Selfishness, greed of the soul (shuhh) and selflessness
themes.note: Musa's and Isa's peoples divided because they became self-centred rather than nation-centred, and rejected Ahmad rather than give anything up.

themes.label: Significance and etiquettes of Jumuah
themes.note: Jumuah is Islam's installed system of leadership and weekly message to a billion people; Muslims have emptied it into a skeleton.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: Leadership comes pre-installed through Jumuah: whoever gives the khutbah is the one who leads and decides for the community.

themes.label: Public speaking and khutbah delivery

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it

69:3.en: Ah, what will convey unto thee what the reality is

69:4.en: (The tribes of) Thamud and A'ad disbelieved in the judgment to come

69:5.en: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the lightning

69:6.ar: وَأَمَّا عَادࣱ فَأُهۡلِكُواْ بِرِيحࣲ صَرۡصَرٍ عَاتِيَةࣲ‏
69:6.en: And as for A'ad, they were destroyed by a fierce roaring wind

69:7.ar: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ سَبۡعَ لَيَالࣲ وَثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومࣰ اۖ فَتَرَى ٱلۡقَوۡمَ فِيهَا صَرۡعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمۡ أَعۡجَازُ نَخۡلٍ خَاوِيَةࣲ‏
69:7.en: Which He imposed on them for seven long nights and eight long days so that thou mightest have seen men lying overthrown, as they were hollow trunks of palm-trees

69:8.en: Canst thou (O Muhammad) see any remnant of them

69:9.ar: وَجَآءَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ وَمَن قَبۡلَهُۥ وَٱلۡمُؤۡتَفِكَٰتُ بِٱلۡخَاطِئَةِ
69:9.en: And Pharaoh and those before him, and the communities that were destroyed, brought error

69:10.ar: فَعَصَوۡاْ رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمۡ فَأَخَذَهُمۡ أَخۡذَةࣰ رَّابِيَةً
69:10.en: And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, therefor did He grip them with a tightening grip

69:11.ar: إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا ٱلۡمَآءُ حَمَلۡنَٰكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡجَارِيَةِ
69:11.en: Lo! when the waters rose, We carried you upon the ship

69:12.ar: لِنَجۡعَلَهَا لَكُمۡ تَذۡكِرَةࣰ وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنࣱ وَٰعِيَةࣱ‏
69:12.en: That We might make it a memorial for you, and that remembering ears (that heard the story) might remember

69:13.ar: فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ نَفۡخَةࣱ وَٰحِدَةࣱ‏
69:13.en: And when the trumpet shall sound one blast

69:14.ar: وَحُمِلَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَٱلۡجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ‏
69:14.en: And the earth with the mountains shall be lifted up and crushed with one crash

69:15.en: Then, on that day will the Event befall

69:16.en: And the heaven will split asunder, for that day it will be frail

69:17.ar: وَٱلۡمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرۡجَآئِهَاۚ وَيَحۡمِلُ عَرۡشَ رَبِّكَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ ثَمَٰنِيَةࣱ‏
69:17.en: And the angels will be on the sides thereof, and eight will uphold the Throne of thy Lord that day, above them

69:18.ar: يَوۡمَئِذࣲ تُعۡرَضُونَ لَا تَخۡفَىٰ مِنكُمۡ خَافِيَةࣱ‏
69:18.en: On that day ye will be exposed; not a secret of you will be hidden

69:19.ar: فَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ هَآؤُمُ ٱقۡرَءُواْ كِتَٰبِيَهۡ
69:19.en: Then, as for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: Take, read my book

69:20.en: Surely I knew that I should have to meet my reckoning

69:21.en: Then he will be in blissful state

69:23.en: Whereof the clusters are in easy reach

69:24.ar: كُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ هَنِيٓـَٔۢا بِمَآ أَسۡلَفۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَيَّامِ ٱلۡخَالِيَةِ
69:24.en: (And it will be said unto those therein): Eat and drink at ease for that which ye sent on before you in past days

69:25.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِشِمَالِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أُوتَ كِتَٰبِيَهۡ
69:25.en: But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: Oh, would that I had not been given my book

69:26.en: And knew not what my reckoning

69:27.en: Oh, would that it had been death

69:28.en: My wealth hath not availed me

69:29.en: My power hath gone from me

69:30.en: (It will be said): Take him and fetter him

69:31.en: And then expose him to hell-fire

69:32.ar: ثُمَّ فِي سِلۡسِلَةࣲ ذَرۡعُهَا سَبۡعُونَ ذِرَاعࣰ ا فَٱسۡلُكُوهُ
69:32.en: And then insert him in a chain whereof the length is seventy cubits

69:33.ar: إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
69:33.en: Lo! He used not to believe in Allah the Tremendous

69:34.en: And urged not on the feeding of the wretched

69:35.en: Therefor hath he no lover here this day

69:38.en: But nay! I swear by all that ye see

69:39.en: And all that ye see not

69:40.en: That it is indeed the speech of an illustrious messenger

69:41.ar: وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوۡلِ شَاعِرࣲۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تُؤۡمِنُونَ
69:41.en: It is not poet's speech - little is it that ye believe

69:42.ar: وَلَا بِقَوۡلِ كَاهِنࣲۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
69:42.en: Nor diviner's speech - little is it that ye remember

69:43.en: It is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds

69:44.en: And if he had invented false sayings concerning Us

69:45.en: We assuredly had taken him by the right hand

69:47.ar: فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنۡ أَحَدٍ عَنۡهُ حَٰجِزِينَ
69:47.en: And not one of you could have held Us off from him

69:48.en: And lo! it is a warrant unto those who ward off (evil)

69:49.en: And lo! We know that some among you will deny (it)

69:50.en: And lo! it is indeed an anguish for the disbelievers

69:51.en: And lo! it is absolute truth

69:52.en: So glorify the name of thy Tremendous Lord

7mnMg3zx_6o.speaker: adnan
7mnMg3zx_6o.speaker_note: Surah Summaries series; links the surah to the previous surahs he covered in the same cluster
7mnMg3zx_6o.title: Surat Al-Haqqah Summary
7mnMg3zx_6o.one_line: Al-Haqqah supplies the emotional element of dawah: stories and Judgment scenes that stir hope, fear and reverence, binding belief to behaviour.
7mnMg3zx_6o.summary: He frames the first surahs of this cluster as four things a person needs to call to Islam: knowledge, values, and here remembrance, the emotional and spiritual attachment without which faith turns cold and eventually fades, like a marriage without love. Al-Haqqah, the ultimate truth, opens with questions meant to make you wonder, then recounts Thamud's sudden blast, Ad's seven nights of wind leaving bodies like hollow palm trunks, Pharaoh, and the ark of Nuh, as reminders for a conscious ear. He explains that hope of mercy and fear of punishment are strong motives that make obeying easier. The Day itself: the heavens torn, eight bearing the Throne, every secret exposed. The one given his book in his right hand wants everyone to read it; the one given it in his left wishes he had never been accountable at all and finds his wealth and status useless. He dwells on the two reasons named for punishment: not believing in Allah and not urging the feeding of the poor. The Quran never punishes for belief alone, he argues, so separating creed from conduct makes religion harmful. The closing verse on what would happen if the Prophet fabricated even a word instils reverence, ending in certainty and glorification.

outline.heading: Opening
Four things needed for dawah
outline.gist: Knowledge, values and ethics, and remembrance: an emotional and spiritual connection, each covered by a surah of this cluster.

outline.heading: Knowledge and ethics without spirit go cold
outline.gist: Some people know a lot and behave well but feel nothing, and without attachment they eventually tire and drift away.

outline.heading: Remembrance and the name Al-Haqqah
outline.gist: The surah moves the reader through history and Judgment; its name intensifies the root for truth to mean the ultimate truth.

outline.heading: 'What is al-Haqqah?' Questions that engage
outline.gist: The Quranic question draws you into wondering, stimulating emotion and attachment beyond knowledge and ritual.

outline.heading: Like a marriage without love
outline.gist: Two good people with good values can still drift apart when affection is missing; faith without feeling fades the same way.

outline.heading: Thamud struck by a sudden blast
outline.gist: The surah begins its historical account with Thamud's swift, violent punishment.

outline.heading: Ad, Pharaoh and the ark of Nuh
outline.gist: Ad were battered for seven nights and eight days and left like hollow palm trunks; Pharaoh and the overturned towns were seized; believers were carried in the ark.

outline.heading: A reminder for a conscious ear
outline.gist: These stories need a listener aware enough to let them reach the soul and change behaviour.

outline.heading: Interlude
Hope and fear as motives
outline.gist: Love, desire, fear and reverence define human experience and make following Allah's word easier.

outline.heading: The Event: the heavens torn, eight bear the Throne, all exposed
outline.gist: The once-magnificent cosmos becomes frail, angels stand at its edges, and everything public and secret is laid bare.

outline.heading: Book in the right hand: 'come read my book'
outline.gist: The successful person wants to share his joy, showing forgiven sins and accepted deeds.

outline.heading: He prepared for this day: a pleasing life
outline.gist: He knew he would meet his account; now he lives calmly in a lofty garden and is told to enjoy what he worked for.

outline.heading: Book in the left hand: wishing he were never accountable
outline.gist: He wishes he had lived like an animal without responsibility; his wealth, connections and power are gone.

outline.heading: Seize him: unbelief and not urging food for the poor
outline.gist: After a graphic description of chains, the two reasons given are not believing in Allah and not encouraging the feeding of the needy.

outline.heading: The Quran never punishes for belief alone
outline.gist: Every punishment mentioned involves conduct toward others; Islam is beliefs plus a way of living with people and the earth.

outline.heading: Belief without action becomes harmful
outline.gist: Certainty without practice breeds arrogance; reading the Quran keeps the two joined.

outline.heading: Interlude
Paradise and punishment both need belief and behaviour
outline.gist: People like to disconnect creed from care for the world because it is easier, but the Quran does not support that narrative.

outline.heading: No friend, no food; an oath by what you see and do not see
outline.gist: Only the wrongdoers end there; Allah swears that this is the word of a noble messenger.

outline.heading: Not poetry, not sorcery: a reminder from the Lord of all
outline.gist: They reject it not from doubt but from not wanting to be reminded.

outline.heading: Had he fabricated a single word
outline.gist: Allah would have seized the Prophet and cut his aorta at once, and no one could stop it; he never did.

outline.heading: Reverence alongside understanding
outline.gist: The verse instils fear and respect, the feeling that this is serious and real, which must accompany comprehension.

outline.heading: Certain truth: glorify your Lord
outline.gist: Haqq al-yaqin is certainty so complete it becomes lived experience; the surah builds emotion so the final glorification comes from the heart.

outline.heading: Outro

67:1.ar: تَبَٰرَكَ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
67:1.en: Blessed is He in Whose hand is the Sovereignty, and, He is Able to do all things

67:2.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ أَيُّكُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلࣰ اۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ
67:2.en: Who hath created life and death that He may try you which of you is best in conduct; and He is the Mighty, the Forgiving

67:3.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ طِبَاقࣰ اۖ مَّا تَرَىٰ فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ مِن تَفَٰوُتࣲۖ فَٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ هَلۡ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورࣲ‏
67:3.en: Who hath created seven heavens in harmony. Thou (Muhammad) canst see no fault in the Beneficent One's creation; then look again: Canst thou see any rifts

67:4.ar: ثُمَّ ٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيۡنِ يَنقَلِبۡ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡبَصَرُ خَاسِئࣰ ا وَهُوَ حَسِيرࣱ‏
67:4.en: Then look again and yet again, thy sight will return unto thee weakened and made dim

67:5.ar: وَلَقَدۡ زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا بِمَصَٰبِيحَ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهَا رُجُومࣰ ا لِّلشَّيَٰطِينِۖ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:5.en: And verily We have beautified the world's heaven with lamps, and We have made them missiles for the devils, and for them We have prepared the doom of flame

67:6.ar: وَلِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمۡ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
67:6.en: And for those who disbelieve in their Lord there is the doom of hell, a hapless journey's end

67:7.ar: إِذَآ أُلۡقُواْ فِيهَا سَمِعُواْ لَهَا شَهِيقࣰ ا وَهِيَ تَفُورُ
67:7.en: When they are flung therein they hear its roaring as it boileth up

67:8.ar: تَكَادُ تَمَيَّزُ مِنَ ٱلۡغَيۡظِۖ كُلَّمَآ أُلۡقِيَ فِيهَا فَوۡجࣱ سَأَلَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَآ أَلَمۡ يَأۡتِكُمۡ نَذِيرࣱ‏
67:8.en: As it would burst with rage. Whenever a (fresh) host is flung therein the wardens thereof ask them: Came there unto you no warner

67:9.ar: قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ قَدۡ جَآءَنَا نَذِيرࣱ فَكَذَّبۡنَا وَقُلۡنَا مَا نَزَّلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ كَبِيرࣲ‏
67:9.en: They say: Yea, verily, a warner came unto us; but we denied and said: Allah hath naught revealed; ye are in naught but a great error

67:10.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡ كُنَّا نَسۡمَعُ أَوۡ نَعۡقِلُ مَا كُنَّا فِيٓ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:10.en: And they say: Had we been wont to listen or have sense, we had not been among the dwellers in the flames

67:11.ar: فَٱعۡتَرَفُواْ بِذَنۢبِهِمۡ فَسُحۡقࣰ ا لِّأَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:11.en: So they acknowledge their sins; but far removed (from mercy) are the dwellers in the flames

67:12.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣱ وَأَجۡرࣱ كَبِيرࣱ‏
67:12.en: Lo! those who fear their Lord in secret, theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward

67:13.ar: وَأَسِرُّواْ قَوۡلَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱجۡهَرُواْ بِهِۦٓۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
67:13.en: And keep your opinion secret or proclaim it, lo! He is Knower of all that is in the breasts (of men)

67:14.ar: أَلَا يَعۡلَمُ مَنۡ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
67:14.en: Should He not know what He created? And He is the Subtile, the Aware

67:15.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ ذَلُولࣰ ا فَٱمۡشُواْ فِي مَنَاكِبِهَا وَكُلُواْ مِن رِّزۡقِهِۦۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلنُّشُورُ
67:15.en: He it is Who hath made the earth subservient unto you, so Walk in the paths thereof and eat of His providence. And unto Him will be the resurrection (of the dead)

67:16.ar: ءَأَمِنتُم مَّن فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يَخۡسِفَ بِكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَمُورُ
67:16.en: Have ye taken security from Him Who is in the heaven that He will not cause the earth to swallow you when lo! it is convulsed

67:17.ar: أَمۡ أَمِنتُم مَّن فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يُرۡسِلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حَاصِبࣰ اۖ فَسَتَعۡلَمُونَ كَيۡفَ نَذِيرِ
67:17.en: Or have ye taken security from Him Who is in the heaven that He will not let loose on you a hurricane? But ye shall know the manner of My warning

67:18.ar: وَلَقَدۡ كَذَّبَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ فَكَيۡفَ كَانَ نَكِيرِ
67:18.en: And verily those before them denied, then (see) the manner of My wrath (with them)

67:19.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ إِلَى ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَوۡقَهُمۡ صَٰٓفَّٰتࣲ وَيَقۡبِضۡنَۚ مَا يُمۡسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُۚ إِنَّهُۥ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءِۭ بَصِيرٌ
67:19.en: Have they not seen the birds above them spreading out their wings and closing them? Naught upholdeth them save the Beneficent. Lo! He is Seer of all things

67:20.ar: أَمَّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ جُندࣱ لَّكُمۡ يَنصُرُكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِۚ إِنِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ إِلَّا فِي غُرُورٍ
67:20.en: Or who is he that will be an army unto you to help you instead of the Beneficent? The disbelievers are in naught but illusion

67:21.ar: أَمَّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي يَرۡزُقُكُمۡ إِنۡ أَمۡسَكَ رِزۡقَهُۥۚ بَل لَّجُّواْ فِي عُتُوࣲّ وَنُفُورٍ
67:21.en: Or who is he that will provide for you if He should withhold His providence? Nay, but they are set in pride and frowardness

67:22.ar: أَفَمَن يَمۡشِي مُكِبًّا عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦٓ أَهۡدَىٰٓ أَمَّن يَمۡشِي سَوِيًّا عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
67:22.en: Is he who goeth groping on his face more rightly guided, or he who walketh upright on a straight road

67:23.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنشَأَكُمۡ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرَ وَٱلۡأَفۡـِٔدَةَۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تَشۡكُرُونَ
67:23.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): He it is who gave you being, and hath assigned unto you ears and eyes and hearts. Small thanks give ye

67:24.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱلَّذِي ذَرَأَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
67:24.en: Say: He it is Who multiplieth you in the earth, and unto Whom ye will be gathered

67:25.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلۡوَعۡدُ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
67:25.en: And they say: When (will) this promise (be fulfilled), if ye are truthful

67:26.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّمَا ٱلۡعِلۡمُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَإِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
67:26.en: Say: The knowledge is with Allah only, and I am but a plain warner

67:27.ar: فَلَمَّا رَأَوۡهُ زُلۡفَةࣰ سِيٓـَٔتۡ وُجُوهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَقِيلَ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَدَّعُونَ
67:27.en: But when they see it nigh, the faces of those who disbelieve will be awry, and it will be said (unto them): This is that for which ye used to call

67:28.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِنۡ أَهۡلَكَنِيَ ٱللَّهُ وَمَن مَّعِيَ أَوۡ رَحِمَنَا فَمَن يُجِيرُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ مِنۡ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
67:28.en: Say (O Muhammad): Have ye thought: Whether Allah causeth me (Muhammad) and those with me to perish or hath mercy on us, still, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful doom

67:29.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ وَعَلَيۡهِ تَوَكَّلۡنَاۖ فَسَتَعۡلَمُونَ مَنۡ هُوَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
67:29.en: Say: He is the Beneficent. In Him we believe and in Him we put our trust. And ye will soon know who it is that is in error manifest

67:30.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِنۡ أَصۡبَحَ مَآؤُكُمۡ غَوۡرࣰ ا فَمَن يَأۡتِيكُم بِمَآءࣲ مَّعِينِۭ
67:30.en: Say: Have ye thought: If (all) your water were to disappear into the earth, who then could bring you gushing water
