BRTO67lb0TY.title: Surat Al-Mulk Summary
BRTO67lb0TY.one_line: Opening the Juz 29 cluster on what a caller to Allah needs, Al-Mulk gives the core knowledge: Allah's dominion, life as a test, accountability and dependence.
BRTO67lb0TY.summary: He introduces Juz 29 as a cluster about dawah: what a person who calls others to Allah needs in knowledge, ethics, connection and behaviour, and Al-Mulk supplies the knowledge. The first verses establish that dominion and endless blessing belong to Allah and answer humanity's oldest question: life and death were created to test who acts best, a clarity many people never find. Allah's name al-Aziz marks the point where our questions stop. The seamless heavens show one set of laws, pointing to one Creator. He explains why warnings of Hell outnumber promises of Paradise: people have a greater right to be told the consequence of failure than the reward of success. Allah knows what is hidden in hearts, provides and protects, and there is no basis for the false sense of security of those who ignore Him; history shows what happened to nations who refused. Walking with one's head up is the image of knowledge giving perspective. He warns Muslims against obsessing over the timing and signs of the Hour or over who will enter Paradise or Hell: neither is our business, our own destination is. The surah closes on dependence on Allah for something as basic as flowing water. He urges memorizing the surah and letting this knowledge show in behaviour.

outline.heading: Juz 29 cluster: what the caller to Allah needs
outline.gist: These surahs condense what a person calling to Allah needs, in tools, methods and examples; representing Islam and calling to it is the point of being Muslim.

outline.heading: Al-Mulk: the knowledge you must be certain of
outline.gist: Each surah of the cluster covers one need; Al-Mulk covers the knowledge a Muslim must hold with certainty and pass on.

outline.heading: The virtues of Surah Al-Mulk
outline.gist: Authentic narrations describe it protecting from the punishment of the grave and on Judgment Day, encouraging nightly recitation, memorization and living its message.

outline.heading: Tabarak: endless blessing and dominion in His hand
outline.gist: The first verse tells us blessing from Allah is limitless, sovereignty is His and He is capable of all things.

outline.heading: Why we live and die: to be tested
outline.gist: The second verse answers the eternal question directly: life is a series of trials in which we show perseverance, strength and gratitude and return to Allah; many people live aimlessly without this answer.

outline.heading: Al-Aziz: where the last 'why' stops
outline.gist: Asking why there must be a test at all reaches the point that is Allah's choice; He is not questioned.

outline.heading: Seven heavens, one system
outline.gist: Look again and again and you find no flaw or second set of laws; the oneness of the laws points to the oneness of Allah.

outline.heading: Hell nearly bursting with rage and the late admission
outline.gist: The people of the Fire admit a warner came and they refused; had they listened and reflected they would not be there, but admission is now too late.

outline.heading: Those who fear their Lord unseen
outline.gist: The other side of the coin: forgiveness and great reward for those who revere Allah without seeing Him.

outline.heading: Why warning outweighs good news
outline.gist: There are many verses on Hell and one on Paradise because people have the right to know the consequence of failure; a reward nobody mentioned is a pleasant surprise, a punishment nobody warned of is a betrayal.

outline.heading: The All-Knowing and the Subtle
outline.gist: Secret or open speech makes no difference; the Creator knows what He created, including thoughts and emotions with no outward footprint.

outline.heading: Interlude
The basics of creed: no protector or provider but Allah
outline.gist: The surah keeps to essentials: who Allah is, the basic rules He set, and reward and punishment.

outline.heading: Where does your false sense of security come from?
outline.gist: Living as if there is no purpose assumes safety from Allah, who owns everything; this is logic more than threat, and the history of earlier nations shows the outcome.

outline.heading: The earth made easy: explore and enjoy, but remember
outline.gist: Walk its paths and eat its provision, remembering you return to Him and that only He provides and protects.

outline.heading: Face to the ground or head up
outline.gist: Knowledge lifts the head to see the path, the ending and the reason we are here; without it a person sees only what they have and lack.

outline.heading: Hearing, sight and hearts: owing gratitude
outline.gist: The faculties and life itself are blessings that demand thanks.

outline.heading: When is the Hour? Not your business
outline.gist: The disbelievers' question is superficial; what matters is preparation. Muslims overinvest in timing and signs of the end, which the Quran leaves to Allah.

outline.heading: The faces of the deniers, and 'what about you?'
outline.gist: When it comes near their faces darken; whether Allah destroys or shows mercy to the believers, the deniers still have no protection.

outline.heading: Stop asking who is going to Paradise or Hell
outline.gist: Fixation on other people's destination is a trait of the disbelievers that Muslims have picked up; Allah gave no one that ministry, and our task is our own destination.

outline.heading: We believe in the Most Merciful and rely on Him
outline.gist: The final statement of belief and reliance, and wait to see who is misguided.

outline.heading: If your water sank away
outline.gist: Humans could only exist because Allah placed flowing water on earth before we could build dams and reservoirs; if He removes it no one else can restore it.

outline.heading: Knowledge that shows in behaviour
outline.gist: The one who represents Allah must know these truths and reflect them in conduct; the coming surahs address ethics, emotions and behaviour.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah
themes.note: Dominion, power, oneness of creation's laws and complete knowledge are the core facts about Allah the surah teaches.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Life and death exist to test who acts best; Muslims are given the answer others search for.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Hell's people confess too late; warnings outweigh good news because people deserve to know consequences.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: The Juz 29 cluster is about what the caller to Allah needs, and Al-Mulk provides the knowledge.

themes.label: Priorities in the deen: fundamentals before details
themes.note: Do not waste time on the timing and signs of the Hour or on judging others' destinations; focus on your own preparation.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Only Allah protects and provides, so the security of the heedless is false.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Dependence on Allah even for flowing water.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Hearing, sight and consciousness call for gratitude.

hadith.gist: Surah Al-Mulk protects its reciter from the punishment of the grave and intercedes on Judgment Day

maxims: The point of being Muslim is to represent Islam
The more knowledge you have, your head goes up
The timing of the Hour is not your business
Figure out where you are going, not others
contemporary: Muslim fixation on the major signs of the Hour
Muslims judging who will enter Paradise or Hell
takeaways: Memorize and recite Surah Al-Mulk regularly
Treat every trial as part of the test you were created for
Spend less time on end-times speculation and more on preparing
Stop judging other people's destination and work on your own
Let knowledge of Allah show in your behaviour when you represent Islam

37:1.en: By those who set the ranks in battle order

37:2.en: And those who drive away (the wicked) with reproof

37:3.en: And those who read (the Word) for a reminder

37:4.en: Lo! thy Lord is surely One

37:5.ar: رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا وَرَبُّ ٱلۡمَشَٰرِقِ
37:5.en: Lord of the heavens and of the earth and all that is between them, and Lord of the sun's risings

37:6.ar: إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا بِزِينَةٍ ٱلۡكَوَاكِبِ
37:6.en: Lo! We have adorned the lowest heaven with an ornament, the planets

37:7.ar: وَحِفۡظࣰ ا مِّن كُلِّ شَيۡطَٰنࣲ مَّارِدࣲ‏
37:7.en: With security from every froward devil

37:8.ar: لَّا يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡمَلَإِ ٱلۡأَعۡلَىٰ وَيُقۡذَفُونَ مِن كُلِّ جَانِبࣲ‏
37:8.en: They cannot listen to the Highest Chiefs for they are pelted from every side

37:9.en: Outcast, and theirs is a perpetual torment

37:10.ar: إِلَّا مَنۡ خَطِفَ ٱلۡخَطۡفَةَ فَأَتۡبَعَهُۥ شِهَابࣱ ثَاقِبࣱ‏
37:10.en: Save him who snatcheth a fragment, and there pursueth him a piercing flame

37:11.ar: فَٱسۡتَفۡتِهِمۡ أَهُمۡ أَشَدُّ خَلۡقًا أَم مَّنۡ خَلَقۡنَآۚ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰهُم مِّن طِينࣲ لَّازِبِۭ
37:11.en: Then ask them (O Muhammad): Are they stronger as a creation, or those (others) whom we have created? Lo! We created them of plastic clay

37:12.en: Nay, but thou dost marvel when they mock

37:13.en: And heed not when they are reminded

37:14.en: And seek to scoff when they behold a portent

37:15.ar: وَقَالُوٓاْ إِنۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحۡرࣱ مُّبِينٌ
37:15.en: And they say: Lo! this is mere magic

37:16.ar: أَءِذَا مِتۡنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابࣰ ا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبۡعُوثُونَ
37:16.en: When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we then, forsooth, be raised (again)

37:18.en: Say (O Muhammad): Ye, in truth; and ye will be brought low

37:19.ar: فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ زَجۡرَةࣱ وَٰحِدَةࣱ فَإِذَا هُمۡ يَنظُرُونَ
37:19.en: There is but one Shout, and lo! they behold

37:20.en: And say: Ah, woe for us! This is the Day of Judgment

37:21.ar: هَٰذَا يَوۡمُ ٱلۡفَصۡلِ ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِۦ تُكَذِّبُونَ
37:21.en: This is the Day of Separation, which ye used to deny

37:22.ar: ۞ٱحۡشُرُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ وَأَزۡوَٰجَهُمۡ وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡبُدُونَ
37:22.en: (And it is said unto the angels): Assemble those who did wrong, together with their wives and what they used to worship

37:23.ar: مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَٱهۡدُوهُمۡ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطِ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
37:23.en: Instead of Allah, and lead them to the path to hell

37:24.en: And stop them, for they must be questioned

37:25.en: What aileth you that ye help not one another

37:26.en: Nay, but this day they make full submission

37:27.en: And some of them draw near unto others, mutually questioning

37:28.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَأۡتُونَنَا عَنِ ٱلۡيَمِينِ
37:28.en: They say: Lo! ye used to come unto us, imposing, (swearing that ye spoke the truth)

37:29.en: They answer: Nay, but ye (yourselves) were not believers

37:30.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لَنَا عَلَيۡكُم مِّن سُلۡطَٰنِۭۖ بَلۡ كُنتُمۡ قَوۡمࣰ ا طَٰغِينَ
37:30.en: We had no power over you, but ye were wayward folk

37:31.ar: فَحَقَّ عَلَيۡنَا قَوۡلُ رَبِّنَآۖ إِنَّا لَذَآئِقُونَ
37:31.en: Now the Word of our Lord hath been fulfilled concerning us. Lo! we are about to taste (the doom)

37:32.en: Thus we misled you. Lo! we were (ourselves) astray

37:33.en: Then lo! this day they (both) are sharers in the doom

37:34.en: Lo! thus deal We with the guilty

37:35.ar: إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُوٓاْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ
37:35.en: For when it was said unto them, There is no Allah save Allah, they were scornful

37:36.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ أَئِنَّا لَتَارِكُوٓاْ ءَالِهَتِنَا لِشَاعِرࣲ مَّجۡنُونِۭ
37:36.en: And said: Shall we forsake our gods for a mad poet

37:37.en: Nay, but he brought the Truth, and he confirmed those sent (before him)

37:38.en: Lo! (now) verily ye taste the painful doom

37:39.ar: وَمَا تُجۡزَوۡنَ إِلَّا مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
37:39.en: Ye are requited naught save what ye did

37:41.en: For them there is a known provision

37:42.en: Fruits. And they will be honoured

37:45.en: A cup from a gushing spring is brought round for them

37:47.ar: لَا فِيهَا غَوۡلࣱ وَلَا هُمۡ عَنۡهَا يُنزَفُونَ
37:47.en: Wherein there is no headache nor are they made mad thereby

37:48.en: And with them are those of modest gaze, with lovely eyes

37:49.en: (Pure) as they were hidden eggs (of the ostrich)

37:50.en: And some of them draw near unto others, mutually questioning

37:51.ar: قَالَ قَآئِلࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ إِنِّي كَانَ لِي قَرِينࣱ‏
37:51.en: A speaker of them saith: Lo! I had a comrade

37:52.en: Who used to say: Art thou in truth of those who put faith (in his words)

37:53.ar: أَءِذَا مِتۡنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابࣰ ا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَدِينُونَ
37:53.en: Can we, when we are dead and have become mere dust and bones - can we (then) verily be brought to book

37:55.en: Then looketh he and seeth him in the depth of hell

37:56.en: He saith: By Allah, thou verily didst all but cause my ruin

37:57.ar: وَلَوۡلَا نِعۡمَةُ رَبِّي لَكُنتُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُحۡضَرِينَ
37:57.en: And had it not been for the favour of my Lord, I too had been of those haled forth (to doom)

37:58.en: Are we then not to die

37:59.ar: إِلَّا مَوۡتَتَنَا ٱلۡأُولَىٰ وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ
37:59.en: Saving our former death, and are we not to be punished

37:60.en: Lo! this is the supreme triumph

37:61.en: For the like of this, then, let the workers work

37:75.en: And Noah verily prayed unto Us, and gracious was the Hearer of his prayer

37:76.en: And We saved him and his household from the great distress

37:77.en: And made his seed the survivors

37:78.en: And left for him among the later folk (the salutation)

37:79.en: Peace be unto Noah among the peoples

37:80.en: Lo! thus do We reward the good

37:81.en: Lo! he is one of Our believing slaves

37:82.en: Then We did drown the others

37:100.en: My Lord! Vouchsafe me of the righteous

37:101.en: So We gave him tidings of a gentle son

37:102.ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعۡيَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰ فِي ٱلۡمَنَامِ أَنِّيٓ أَذۡبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرَىٰۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفۡعَلۡ مَا تُؤۡمَرُۖ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
37:102.en: And when (his son) was old enough to walk with him, (Abraham) said: O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee. So look, what thinkest thou? He said: O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Allah willing, thou shalt find me of the steadfast

37:103.en: Then, when they had both surrendered (to Allah), and he had flung him down upon his face

37:104.en: We called unto him: O Abraham

37:105.ar: قَدۡ صَدَّقۡتَ ٱلرُّءۡيَآۚ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
37:105.en: Thou hast already fulfilled the vision. Lo! thus do We reward the good

37:106.en: Lo! that verily was a clear test

37:107.en: Then We ransomed him with a tremendous victim

37:114.en: And We verily gave grace unto Moses and Aaron

37:115.en: And saved them and their people from the great distress

37:116.en: And helped them so that they became the victors

37:117.en: And We gave them the clear Scripture

37:118.en: And showed them the right path

37:119.en: And We left for them among the later folk (the salutation)

37:120.en: Peace be unto Moses and Aaron

37:121.en: Lo! thus do We reward the good

37:122.en: Lo! they are two of Our believing slaves

37:123.en: And lo! Elias was of those sent (to warn)

37:124.en: When he said unto his folk: Will ye not ward off (evil)

37:125.ar: أَتَدۡعُونَ بَعۡلࣰ ا وَتَذَرُونَ أَحۡسَنَ ٱلۡخَٰلِقِينَ
37:125.en: Will ye cry unto Baal and forsake the Best of creators

37:126.en: Allah, your Lord and Lord of your forefathers

37:127.en: But they denied him, so they surely will be haled forth (to the doom)

37:129.en: And we left for him among the later folk (the salutation)

37:131.en: Lo! thus do We reward the good

37:132.en: Lo! he is one of our believing slaves

37:133.en: And lo! Lot verily was of those sent (to warn)

37:134.en: When We saved him and his household, every one

37:135.en: Save an old woman among those who stayed behind

37:137.en: And lo! ye verily pass by (the ruin of) them in the morning

37:138.en: And at night-time; have ye then no sense

37:139.en: And lo! Jonah verily was of those sent (to warn)

37:140.en: When he fled unto the laden ship

37:141.en: And then drew lots and was of those rejected

37:142.en: And the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy

37:143.en: And had he not been one of those who glorify (Allah)

37:144.ar: لَلَبِثَ فِي بَطۡنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ يُبۡعَثُونَ
37:144.en: He would have tarried in its belly till the day when they are raised

37:145.en: Then We cast him on a desert shore while he was sick

37:146.en: And We caused a tree of gourd to grow above him

37:147.ar: وَأَرۡسَلۡنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ مِاْئَةِ أَلۡفٍ أَوۡ يَزِيدُونَ
37:147.en: And We sent him to a hundred thousand (folk) or more

37:148.en: And they believed, therefor We gave them comfort for a while

37:62.ar: أَذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرࣱ نُّزُلًا أَمۡ شَجَرَةُ ٱلزَّقُّومِ
37:62.en: Is this better as a welcome, or the tree of Zaqqum

37:63.en: Lo! We have appointed it a torment for wrong-doers

37:64.ar: إِنَّهَا شَجَرَةࣱ تَخۡرُجُ فِيٓ أَصۡلِ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
37:64.en: Lo! it is a tree that springeth in the heart of hell

37:65.en: Its crop is as it were the heads of devils

37:66.ar: فَإِنَّهُمۡ لَأٓكِلُونَ مِنۡهَا فَمَالِـُٔونَ مِنۡهَا ٱلۡبُطُونَ
37:66.en: And lo! they verily must eat thereof, and fill (their) bellies therewith

37:149.en: Now ask them (O Muhammad): Hath thy Lord daughters whereas they have sons

37:150.ar: أَمۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ إِنَٰثࣰ ا وَهُمۡ شَٰهِدُونَ
37:150.en: Or created We the angels females while they were present

37:151.en: Lo! it is of their falsehood that they say

37:152.en: Allah hath begotten. Allah! verily they tell a lie

37:153.en: (And again of their falsehood): He hath preferred daughters to sons

37:154.en: What aileth you? How judge ye

37:156.en: Or have ye a clear warrant

37:157.en: Then produce your writ, if ye are truthful

37:158.ar: وَجَعَلُواْ بَيۡنَهُۥ وَبَيۡنَ ٱلۡجِنَّةِ نَسَبࣰ اۚ وَلَقَدۡ عَلِمَتِ ٱلۡجِنَّةُ إِنَّهُمۡ لَمُحۡضَرُونَ
37:158.en: And they imagine kinship between him and the jinn, whereas the jinn know well that they will be brought before (Him)

37:159.en: Glorified be Allah from that which they attribute (unto Him)

37:180.ar: سُبۡحَٰنَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ ٱلۡعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
37:180.en: Glorified be thy Lord, the Lord of Majesty, from that which they attribute (unto Him)

37:181.en: And peace be unto those sent (to warn)

37:182.en: And praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds

36:3.en: Lo! thou art of those sent

36:5.en: A revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful

36:6.ar: لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمࣰ ا مَّآ أُنذِرَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ فَهُمۡ غَٰفِلُونَ
36:6.en: That thou mayst warn a folk whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless

36:7.ar: لَقَدۡ حَقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ عَلَىٰٓ أَكۡثَرِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
36:7.en: Already hath the judgment, (for their infidelity) proved true of most of them, for they believe not

36:8.ar: إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا فِيٓ أَعۡنَٰقِهِمۡ أَغۡلَٰلࣰ ا فَهِيَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَذۡقَانِ فَهُم مُّقۡمَحُونَ
36:8.en: Lo! We have put on their necks carcans reaching unto the chins, so that they are made stiff-necked

36:9.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنۢ بَيۡنِ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ سَدࣰّ ا وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ سَدࣰّ ا فَأَغۡشَيۡنَٰهُمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُبۡصِرُونَ
36:9.en: And We have set a bar before them and a bar behind them, and (thus) have covered them so that they see not

36:10.ar: وَسَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
36:10.en: Whether thou warn them or thou warn them not, it is alike for them, for they believe not

lZUyfZvtBbU.speaker: adnan
lZUyfZvtBbU.speaker_note: his Surah Summaries series on the clusters of surahs; recaps his previous night's Ya-Sin session; single teacher throughout
lZUyfZvtBbU.title: Surat As-Saffat Summary
lZUyfZvtBbU.one_line: As-Saffat teaches submission through belief in the unseen and obeying commands whose wisdom we cannot see, illustrated by Nuh, Ibrahim, Ilyas, Lut and Yunus.
lZUyfZvtBbU.summary: He places As-Saffat in the cluster on submission and says its angle is believing in the unseen and obeying commands whose wisdom we cannot see. Islam does not ask for blind faith at the start: people should think, question and seek evidence from the universe, history and revelation until they reach certainty. After that, a person follows Allah's command even without understanding it, provided they are sure it is truly Allah's command and not someone's interpretation or a group's agenda. The surah opens with angels in ranks and the stars that guard the heavens from the jinn, things we can never observe. It shows the resurrected halted and questioned, finally in the submission they refused in life, and a believer in Paradise looking on the friend who mocked belief in the unseen. Its prophets were chosen because each obeyed without seeing the wisdom: Nuh building the ark on a mountain while mocked, Ibrahim and his son submitting to the command to sacrifice, Musa sent toward the sea, little-known Ilyas, Lut on sexual ethics, and Yunus, whose mistake mysteriously saved his people. Allah is not after blood; His actual commands are easy and full of wisdom, yet we still neglect them. Questions like why alcohol, zina or hijab are forbidden begin with the answer that Allah said so. The surah ends by declaring Allah beyond what people imagine.

outline.heading: The cluster on submission to Allah's will
outline.gist: Each surah of the sixth cluster looks at submission from a different angle; submitting is the whole reason we are called Muslims.

outline.heading: Recap of Ya-Sin: life measured by legacy
outline.gist: Obedience and dawah give true life; life is measured not by hours breathed but by the legacy left and the purpose fulfilled.

outline.heading: Reason first: certainty through evidence
outline.gist: Allah wants us to use reason to believe in Him, His creation, revelation and prophets; certainty comes from studying the universe, history and Islam's values.

outline.heading: Then obey, as long as you are sure it is Allah's command
outline.gist: Islam never asked for blind following at the start; after certainty, one obeys even without full understanding, provided it is truly Allah's command and not an agenda or someone's insincere interpretation.

outline.heading: Oath by the angels in ranks
outline.gist: Angels lining up and carrying out Allah's commands are part of the unseen we believe in without contact.

outline.heading: Stars that guard the heavens from the jinn
outline.gist: The jinn cannot overhear the heavens, so Muslims should drop that idea; the stars also have an unseen purpose beyond the observable.

outline.heading: Stop them, they will be questioned
outline.gist: The resurrected are halted and held to account; they cannot help one another and are now in the submission they refused in life.

outline.heading: Interlude
The sincere servants: mukhlasin
outline.gist: The full phrase la ilaha illallah appears rarely; the disbelievers called the Prophet a mad poet, and the word for those Allah purified for Himself recurs in this surah.

outline.heading: The believer in Paradise and the friend who mocked the unseen
outline.gist: A man of Paradise recalls a friend who scoffed at resurrection and looks down to see him in punishment.

outline.heading: Nuh building an ark on a mountain
outline.gist: Mocked as a carpenter who abandoned prophecy, he built it because his certainty in Allah's wisdom let him obey without seeing the reason.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's dream and his son's submission
outline.gist: After waiting long for a forbearing son, Ibrahim was commanded in a dream to sacrifice him, and the son told him to do as commanded. Losing a child is unimaginable.

outline.heading: The ransom: Allah is not after blood
outline.gist: Both fully submitted, and before anything happened Allah called out that the test was passed and ransomed the son with a ram.

outline.heading: Why can't we drink? Because Allah said so, first
outline.gist: Allah's commands are rational and full of wisdom, but we obey whether or not we see it; once you have done your homework on belief, the wisdom unfolds over time.

outline.heading: Interlude
Eid sacrifice: we were given easy commands and still neglect them
outline.gist: Each Eid reminds us Allah never asked us to sacrifice our children; Musa too was told to march to the sea without knowing why.

outline.heading: Ilyas and Lut: the unknown prophet and sexual ethics
outline.gist: We know almost nothing of Ilyas yet accept him as part of the unseen; Lut taught sexual ethics whose wisdom people may only see later.

outline.heading: Yunus: the mistake that saved his people
outline.gist: Had he stayed, his people would have been punished; his error and its punishment led to their salvation, a wisdom no one fully understands.

outline.heading: Two trees: zaqqum and the gourd
outline.gist: The tree of Hell for those who rejected the unseen, and the broad-leafed plant that sheltered Yunus as he recovered; choose your tree.

outline.heading: Allah needs no children
outline.gist: Need for family is human; claims of offspring or kinship between Allah and the jinn are baseless.

outline.heading: Glory to your Lord beyond what they describe
outline.gist: The ending declares Allah beyond imagination; if we could fully understand Him we could challenge Him.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Submission means obeying Allah's commands even when their wisdom is not visible, once certain they are His.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Faith begins with reasoned certainty and includes belief in the unseen: angels, jinn and the purposes of the stars.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Each prophet's story in the surah shows obedience without seeing the wisdom.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The resurrected questioned, and the believer in Paradise seeing his mocking friend.

themes.label: The purposes behind Allah's commands (maqasid)
themes.note: Allah's commands are rational and full of wisdom, but obedience does not wait on understanding it.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Allah needs no offspring and is beyond human imagination.

stories.point: Certainty in Allah lets you obey even when mocked and unable to see the reason.

stories.point: Full submission to the hardest command; Allah's actual commands are merciful and easy.
Allah's wisdom can work through a mistake in ways beyond our grasp.
Accepting what we know little about, and ethical commands whose wisdom appears later.

71:1.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦٓ أَنۡ أَنذِرۡ قَوۡمَكَ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
71:1.en: Lo! We sent Noah unto his people (saying): Warn thy people ere the painful doom come unto them

71:2.ar: قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنِّي لَكُمۡ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينٌ
71:2.en: He said: O my people! Lo! I am a plain warner unto you

71:3.en: (Bidding you): Serve Allah and keep your duty unto Him and obey me

71:4.ar: يَغۡفِرۡ لَكُم مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمۡ وَيُؤَخِّرۡكُمۡ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ مُّسَمًّىۚ إِنَّ أَجَلَ ٱللَّهِ إِذَا جَآءَ لَا يُؤَخَّرُۚ لَوۡ كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
71:4.en: That He may forgive you somewhat of your sins and respite you to an appointed term. Lo! the term of Allah, when it cometh, cannot be delayed, if ye but knew

71:5.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوۡتُ قَوۡمِي لَيۡلࣰ ا وَنَهَارࣰ ا
71:5.en: He said: My Lord! Lo! I have called unto my people night and day

71:6.ar: فَلَمۡ يَزِدۡهُمۡ دُعَآءِيٓ إِلَّا فِرَارࣰ ا
71:6.en: But all my calling doth but add to their repugnance

71:7.ar: وَإِنِّي كُلَّمَا دَعَوۡتُهُمۡ لِتَغۡفِرَ لَهُمۡ جَعَلُوٓاْ أَصَٰبِعَهُمۡ فِيٓ ءَاذَانِهِمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡشَوۡاْ ثِيَابَهُمۡ وَأَصَرُّواْ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ ٱسۡتِكۡبَارࣰ ا
71:7.en: And lo! whenever I call unto them that Thou mayst pardon them they thrust their fingers in their ears and cover themselves with their garments and persist (in their refusal) and magnify themselves in pride

71:8.en: And lo! I have called unto them aloud

71:9.ar: ثُمَّ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَنتُ لَهُمۡ وَأَسۡرَرۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِسۡرَارࣰ ا
71:9.en: And lo! I have made public proclamation unto them, and I have appealed to them in private

71:10.ar: فَقُلۡتُ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارࣰ ا
71:10.en: And I have said: Seek pardon of your Lord. Lo! He was ever Forgiving

71:11.en: He will let loose the sky for you in plenteous rain

71:12.ar: وَيُمۡدِدۡكُم بِأَمۡوَٰلࣲ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ أَنۡهَٰرࣰ ا
71:12.en: And will help you with wealth and sons, and will assign unto you Gardens and will assign unto you rivers

71:13.ar: مَّا لَكُمۡ لَا تَرۡجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَارࣰ ا
71:13.en: What aileth you that ye hope not toward Allah for dignity

71:14.en: When He created you by (divers) stages

71:15.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَوۡاْ كَيۡفَ خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ طِبَاقࣰ ا
71:15.en: See ye not how Allah hath created seven heavens in harmony

71:16.ar: وَجَعَلَ ٱلۡقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورࣰ ا وَجَعَلَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ سِرَاجࣰ ا
71:16.en: And hath made the moon a light therein, and made the sun a lamp

71:17.ar: وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ نَبَاتࣰ ا
71:17.en: And Allah hath caused you to grow as a growth from the earth

71:18.ar: ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمۡ فِيهَا وَيُخۡرِجُكُمۡ إِخۡرَاجࣰ ا
71:18.en: And afterward He maketh you return thereto, and He will bring you forth again, a (new) forthbringing

71:19.ar: وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِسَاطࣰ ا
71:19.en: And Allah hath made the earth a wide expanse for you

71:20.ar: لِّتَسۡلُكُواْ مِنۡهَا سُبُلࣰ ا فِجَاجࣰ ا
71:20.en: That ye may thread the valley-ways thereof

71:21.ar: قَالَ نُوحࣱ رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمۡ عَصَوۡنِي وَٱتَّبَعُواْ مَن لَّمۡ يَزِدۡهُ مَالُهُۥ وَوَلَدُهُۥٓ إِلَّا خَسَارࣰ ا
71:21.en: Noah said: My Lord! Lo! they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children increase him in naught save ruin

71:22.en: And they have plotted a mighty plot

71:23.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَا تَذَرُنَّ ءَالِهَتَكُمۡ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدࣰّ ا وَلَا سُوَاعࣰ ا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسۡرࣰ ا
71:23.en: And they have said: Forsake not your gods. Forsake not Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr

71:24.ar: وَقَدۡ أَضَلُّواْ كَثِيرࣰ اۖ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَٰلࣰ ا
71:24.en: And they have led many astray, and Thou increasest the wrong-doers in naught save error

71:25.ar: مِّمَّا خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِهِمۡ أُغۡرِقُواْ فَأُدۡخِلُواْ نَارࣰ ا فَلَمۡ يَجِدُواْ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَنصَارࣰ ا
71:25.en: Because of their sins they were drowned, then made to enter a Fire. And they found they had no helpers in place of Allah

71:26.ar: وَقَالَ نُوحࣱ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرۡ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا
71:26.en: And Noah said: My Lord! Leave not one of the disbelievers in the land

71:27.ar: إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرۡهُمۡ يُضِلُّواْ عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوٓاْ إِلَّا فَاجِرࣰ ا كَفَّارࣰ ا
71:27.en: If Thou shouldst leave them, they will mislead Thy slaves and will beget none save lewd ingrates

71:28.ar: رَّبِّ ٱغۡفِرۡ لِي وَلِوَٰلِدَيَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيۡتِيَ مُؤۡمِنࣰ ا وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِۖ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارَۢا
71:28.en: My Lord! Forgive me and my parents and him who entereth my house believing, and believing men and believing women, and increase not the wrong-doers in aught save ruin

5:116.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ءَأَنتَ قُلۡتَ لِلنَّاسِ ٱتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّيَ إِلَٰهَيۡنِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۖ قَالَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ مَا يَكُونُ لِيٓ أَنۡ أَقُولَ مَا لَيۡسَ لِي بِحَقٍّۚ إِن كُنتُ قُلۡتُهُۥ فَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَهُۥۚ تَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِي وَلَآ أَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي نَفۡسِكَۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلَّٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ
5:116.en: And when Allah saith: O Jesus, son of Mary! Didst thou say unto mankind: Take me and my mother for two gods beside Allah? he saith: Be glorified! It was not mine to utter that to which I had no right. If I used to say it, then Thou knewest it. Thou knowest what is in my mind, and I know not what is in Thy Mind. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower of Things Hidden

VScz8XD3O7s.speaker: adnan
VScz8XD3O7s.speaker_note: his usual surah-summary format, refers back to his earlier talks in the series
VScz8XD3O7s.title: Surat Nuh Summary
VScz8XD3O7s.one_line: Surah Nuh as a model of dawah: Nuh defends his 950 years of effort in both quantity and quality, teaching us to blame ourselves first.
VScz8XD3O7s.summary: He places Surah Nuh within the cluster of Juz 29 surahs that teach dawah: the earlier ones set out what a Muslim needs (knowledge, values, spiritual connection, behaviour), and Nuh shows dawah done perfectly yet largely rejected. He asks the audience to imagine standing behind Nuh on the Day of Judgment as he prepares his defence for having so few followers after centuries. Nuh first argues quantity: he called his people night and day, publicly and privately, with every method. Then he argues quality: his message told them that seeking forgiveness builds a civilization because it lets people correct mistakes daily, bringing rain, provision, children and wealth, and it pointed them to the creation of the cosmos, the sun and moon, human development in stages and the earth spread out for travel. The sheikh contrasts this rational, relevant, science-rich narrative with much of today's religious messaging, which is trivial, divisive or irrelevant. His central rule: when people do not respond, nine times out of ten the fault is ours, and we must keep revising our methods. Only when Allah told Nuh no one else would believe did he make dua against his people, ending with the dua for his parents and the believers.

outline.heading: Surah Nuh within the dawah cluster of Juz 29
outline.gist: The preceding surahs gave the four categories a Muslim needs for proper dawah; Nuh shows how dawah is done and how it can still fail.

outline.heading: You do your best; acceptance is not in your control
outline.gist: Dawah done properly is our job, while who accepts is beyond us.

outline.heading: Nuh's call: worship, taqwa and obedience
outline.gist: Nuh warns his people and promises forgiveness and respite in return for three things.

outline.heading: 950 years and few believers
outline.gist: Historians put his followers around 83, roughly one person per dozen years, so he must account for the result.

outline.heading: Before blaming people, make sure it was not you
outline.gist: Saying people simply will not accept Islam is a dangerous judgment unless every resource has been exhausted and the work done properly.

outline.heading: Standing behind Nuh on Judgment Day
outline.gist: He asks the audience to imagine Nuh preparing his defence before Allah.

outline.heading: Called night and day; they covered their ears
outline.gist: The more he called them, the more they fled, plugging their ears and covering their faces in arrogance.

outline.heading: Publicly, privately, every method
outline.gist: Nuh's first argument is quantity and variety of method: he never stopped and tried every setting.

outline.heading: Quality of the narrative matters, not just volume
outline.gist: A religious narrative that is irrelevant, biased or answers no real questions makes the caller accountable for people's rejection.

outline.heading: Interlude
Seeking forgiveness builds civilization
outline.gist: Istighfar means identifying and dropping yesterday's mistakes, so individuals and communities improve daily.

outline.heading: Improve and blessings follow: rain, wealth, children
outline.gist: When people treat each other and their environment better, provision increases.

outline.heading: Creation as the evidence for faith
outline.gist: Nuh points to human development in stages, the layered heavens, the sun and moon, humans grown from the earth and the earth spread for travel.

outline.heading: A logical, scientific narrative versus today's preaching
outline.gist: He questions whether narratives lacking logic, relevance and behaviour change, or that spread hatred, will be accepted by Allah.

outline.heading: Nine times out of ten it is your fault
outline.gist: When people do not respond it is our ethical and religious duty to revise everything; even Isa must defend himself before Allah.

outline.heading: Followers of wealth and power; the idols
outline.gist: His people followed a powerful wealthy leader and clung to named idols, each a symbol of a problem we still face.

outline.heading: Drowning and Nuh's dua against his people
outline.gist: Only after Allah told him no more would believe did Nuh pray against them, out of fear for the believers.

outline.heading: Dua for parents and the believers
outline.gist: The closing dua asks forgiveness for his parents, those who entered his house in faith, and all believers.

outline.heading: Keep questioning yourself and changing methods
outline.gist: Unless Allah declares people beyond hope, we live like Nuh: persistent, self-critical, always trying new approaches.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: Dawah must be done properly in quantity and quality; Nuh is the model of persistence and method.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Before blaming the audience, the caller must be sure the failure was not his own.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Nine times out of ten a lack of response is the caller's fault; revise rather than blame society.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Seeking forgiveness is a daily process of correcting mistakes that builds civilization and brings provision.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Nuh's long mission, his defence before Allah and the flood.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Faith should be built on reflection on creation, using science and logic.

themes.label: Mujahadah: striving as a way of life
themes.note: Keep trying harder and changing methods until the very end.

quran.point: Isa is asked whether he told people to worship him and his mother; even a prophet must defend himself.

maxims: Nine times out of ten, it's your fault
It's not just about quantity, it's also about quality
Seeking forgiveness builds a civilization

stories.point: Even a prophet must account for poor results by proving both his effort and his message were sound.
Nuh only gave up on his people when Allah told him none would believe.

contemporary: Muslims running channels about Islam whose content is irrelevant or divisive
takeaways: When people do not respond to your dawah or work, examine yourself and your methods before blaming them.
Make your religious message logical, relevant and grounded in reflection on creation.
Practise istighfar as daily self-correction that makes you better than yesterday.
Vary your approach: publicly, privately, individually and in groups, and never stop.

32:2.ar: تَنزِيلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَا رَيۡبَ فِيهِ مِن رَّبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
32:2.en: The revelation of the Scripture whereof there is no doubt is from the Lord of the Worlds

32:3.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ ٱفۡتَرَىٰهُۚ بَلۡ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمࣰ ا مَّآ أَتَىٰهُم مِّن نَّذِيرࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَهۡتَدُونَ
32:3.en: Or say they: He hath invented it? Nay, but it is the Truth from thy Lord, that thou mayst warn a folk to whom no warner came before thee, that haply they may walk aright

32:4.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ مَا لَكُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ مِن وَلِيࣲّ وَلَا شَفِيعٍۚ أَفَلَا تَتَذَكَّرُونَ
32:4.en: Allah it is Who created the heavens and the earth, and that which is between them, in six Days. Then He mounted the Throne. Ye have not, beside Him, a protecting friend or mediator. Will ye not then remember

32:5.ar: يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ثُمَّ يَعۡرُجُ إِلَيۡهِ فِي يَوۡمࣲ كَانَ مِقۡدَارُهُۥٓ أَلۡفَ سَنَةࣲ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ
32:5.en: He directeth the ordinance from the heaven unto the earth; then it ascendeth unto Him in a Day, whereof the measure is a thousand years of that ye reckon

32:6.ar: ذَٰلِكَ عَٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
32:6.en: Such is the Knower of the Invisible and the Visible, the Mighty, the Merciful

32:7.ar: ٱلَّذِيٓ أَحۡسَنَ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ خَلَقَهُۥۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلۡقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنِ مِن طِينࣲ‏
32:7.en: Who made all things good which He created, and He began the creation of man from clay

32:8.ar: ثُمَّ جَعَلَ نَسۡلَهُۥ مِن سُلَٰلَةࣲ مِّن مَّآءࣲ مَّهِينࣲ‏
32:8.en: Then He made his seed from a draught of despised fluid

32:9.ar: ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِۦۖ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرَ وَٱلۡأَفۡـِٔدَةَۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تَشۡكُرُونَ
32:9.en: Then He fashioned him and breathed into him of His Spirit; and appointed for you hearing and sight and hearts. Small thanks give ye

32:10.ar: وَقَالُوٓاْ أَءِذَا ضَلَلۡنَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَءِنَّا لَفِي خَلۡقࣲ جَدِيدِۭۚ بَلۡ هُم بِلِقَآءِ رَبِّهِمۡ كَٰفِرُونَ
32:10.en: And they say: When we are lost in the earth, how can we then be re-created? Nay but they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord

32:11.ar: ۞قُلۡ يَتَوَفَّىٰكُم مَّلَكُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ ٱلَّذِي وُكِّلَ بِكُمۡ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمۡ تُرۡجَعُونَ
32:11.en: Say: The angel of death, who hath charge concerning you, will gather you, and afterward unto your Lord ye will be returned

32:12.ar: وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ نَاكِسُواْ رُءُوسِهِمۡ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ رَبَّنَآ أَبۡصَرۡنَا وَسَمِعۡنَا فَٱرۡجِعۡنَا نَعۡمَلۡ صَٰلِحًا إِنَّا مُوقِنُونَ
32:12.en: Couldst thou but see when the guilty hang their heads before their Lord, (and say): Our Lord! We have now seen and heard, so send us back; we will do right, now we are sure

32:13.ar: وَلَوۡ شِئۡنَا لَأٓتَيۡنَا كُلَّ نَفۡسٍ هُدَىٰهَا وَلَٰكِنۡ حَقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ مِنِّي لَأَمۡلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ ٱلۡجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجۡمَعِينَ
32:13.en: And if We had so willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me concerning evildoers took effect: that I will fill hell with the jinn and mankind together

32:14.ar: فَذُوقُواْ بِمَا نَسِيتُمۡ لِقَآءَ يَوۡمِكُمۡ هَٰذَآ إِنَّا نَسِينَٰكُمۡۖ وَذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
32:14.en: So taste (the evil of your deeds). Forasmuch as ye forgot the meeting of this your day, lo! We forget you. Taste the doom of immortality because of what ye used to do

32:15.ar: إِنَّمَا يُؤۡمِنُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِهَا خَرُّواْۤ سُجَّدࣰ اۤ وَسَبَّحُواْ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ۩
32:15.en: Only those believe in Our revelations who, when they are reminded of them, fall down prostrate and hymn the praise of their Lord, and they are not scornful

32:16.ar: تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ يَدۡعُونَ رَبَّهُمۡ خَوۡفࣰ ا وَطَمَعࣰ ا وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
32:16.en: Who forsake their beds to cry unto their Lord in fear and hope, and spend of that We have bestowed on them

32:17.ar: فَلَا تَعۡلَمُ نَفۡسࣱ مَّآ أُخۡفِيَ لَهُم مِّن قُرَّةِ أَعۡيُنࣲ جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
32:17.en: No soul knoweth what is kept hid for them of joy, as a reward for what they used to do

32:18.ar: أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤۡمِنࣰ ا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقࣰ اۚ لَّا يَسۡتَوُۥنَ
32:18.en: Is he who is a believer like unto him who is an evil-liver? They are not alike

32:19.ar: أَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَلَهُمۡ جَنَّٰتُ ٱلۡمَأۡوَىٰ نُزُلَۢا بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
32:19.en: But as for those who believe and do good works, for them are the Gardens of Retreat - a welcome (in reward) for what they used to do

32:20.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فَسَقُواْ فَمَأۡوَىٰهُمُ ٱلنَّارُۖ كُلَّمَآ أَرَادُوٓاْ أَن يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَآ أُعِيدُواْ فِيهَا وَقِيلَ لَهُمۡ ذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِۦ تُكَذِّبُونَ
32:20.en: And as for those who do evil, their retreat is the Fire. Whenever they desire to issue forth from thence, they are brought back thither. Unto them it is said: Taste the torment of the Fire which ye used to deny

32:21.ar: وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَدۡنَىٰ دُونَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَكۡبَرِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
32:21.en: And verily We make them taste the lower punishment before the greater, that haply they may return

32:22.ar: وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّن ذُكِّرَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ ثُمَّ أَعۡرَضَ عَنۡهَآۚ إِنَّا مِنَ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ مُنتَقِمُونَ
32:22.en: And who doth greater wrong than he who is reminded of the revelations of his Lord, then turneth from them. Lo! We shall requite the guilty

32:23.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ فَلَا تَكُن فِي مِرۡيَةࣲ مِّن لِّقَآئِهِۦۖ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهُ هُدࣰ ى لِّبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ
32:23.en: We verily gave Moses the Scripture; so be not ye in doubt of his receiving it; and We appointed it a guidance for the Children of Israel

32:24.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡ أَئِمَّةࣰ يَهۡدُونَ بِأَمۡرِنَا لَمَّا صَبَرُواْۖ وَكَانُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يُوقِنُونَ
32:24.en: And when they became steadfast and believed firmly in Our revelations, We appointed from among them leaders who guided by Our command

32:25.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ يَفۡصِلُ بَيۡنَهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ فِيمَا كَانُواْ فِيهِ يَخۡتَلِفُونَ
32:25.en: Lo! thy Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ

32:26.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَهۡدِ لَهُمۡ كَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ يَمۡشُونَ فِي مَسَٰكِنِهِمۡۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتٍۚ أَفَلَا يَسۡمَعُونَ
32:26.en: Is it not a guidance for them (to observe) how many generations We destroyed before them, amid whose dwelling places they do walk? Lo! therein verily are portents! Will they not then heed

32:27.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّا نَسُوقُ ٱلۡمَآءَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلۡجُرُزِ فَنُخۡرِجُ بِهِۦ زَرۡعࣰ ا تَأۡكُلُ مِنۡهُ أَنۡعَٰمُهُمۡ وَأَنفُسُهُمۡۚ أَفَلَا يُبۡصِرُونَ
32:27.en: Have they not seen how We lead the water to the barren land and therewith bring forth crops whereof their cattle eat, and they themselves? Will they not then see

32:28.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلۡفَتۡحُ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
32:28.en: And they say: When cometh this victory (of yours) if ye are truthful

32:29.ar: قُلۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡفَتۡحِ لَا يَنفَعُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِيمَٰنُهُمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يُنظَرُونَ
32:29.en: Say (unto them): On the day of the victory the faith of those who disbelieve (and who then will believe) will not avail them, neither will they be reprieved

32:30.en: So withdraw from them (O Muhammad), and await (the event). Lo! they (also) are awaiting (it)

YI7R-7zrojQ.speaker: adnan
YI7R-7zrojQ.speaker_note: his own surah-summary series; closes the cluster from Al-Qasas to As-Sajdah on relationships
YI7R-7zrojQ.title: Surat As-Sajdah Summary
YI7R-7zrojQ.one_line: As-Sajdah renews our relationship with Allah: He initiated it through His Book and the promised meeting, and we complete it through prostration, night prayer and longing.
YI7R-7zrojQ.summary: Relationships are the most valuable thing we have, yet every relationship slides into routine: marriages, friendships, even the speaker or reciter who used to move you. As-Sajdah closes the cluster on relationships with our relationship with Allah, and we read it every Friday at Fajr to keep it alive. The surah focuses on two articles of faith, the Book and the resurrection, because Quraysh accepted Allah as Creator but denied these, and because any relationship needs communication and a meeting. Allah has initiated His side; He could force everyone to guidance, but a forced relationship is no relationship, so the choice is ours. True believers fall prostrate when reminded, physically or in the heart, and prostration and arrogance cannot live in the same heart. Their sides pull away from their beds out of longing, like an excited child, and they live Allah's law beyond the prayer mat. The believer meets Allah like someone walking in to a manager he knows, while the one who ignored Him comes like a runaway slave. The lesser punishment of worldly troubles is Allah calling us back; there is no refuge from Him except in Him. Whoever refuses the relationship is the only loser.

outline.heading: Relationships are the most valuable thing we have
outline.gist: Nothing in human life has value without relationships.

outline.heading: Every relationship slides into routine
outline.gist: Familiarity dulls marriages and the speakers who once moved us; keeping the spark takes effort.

outline.heading: The cluster on relationships ends with Allah
outline.gist: The surahs from Al-Qasas to As-Sajdah cover our relationships with what surrounds us, and As-Sajdah fittingly closes with our relationship with Allah.

outline.heading: Why we read it every Friday at Fajr
outline.gist: Even a beloved reciter stops moving us; on the day of nearness to Allah, the morning begins with a surah about our relationship with Him.

outline.heading: The Book sent down without doubt
outline.gist: Do they say he invented it? It is the truth from your Lord, to warn a people who had no warner.

outline.heading: When we are lost in the earth, will we be created anew?
outline.gist: They disbelieve in meeting their Lord; the angel of death will take them and return them to Him.

outline.heading: The two articles people struggle with most
outline.gist: Quraysh descended from Ibrahim and believed in God but denied the resurrection and that the Quran was Allah's word; both are Allah initiating a relationship with us.

outline.heading: The opening page: the Book and the resurrection
outline.gist: He walks through the verses in Arabic: bodies consumed and vanished, and the denial of the meeting.

outline.heading: A relationship needs communication and a meeting
outline.gist: Quraysh affirmed Allah as Creator; Allah chose the two articles that define a relationship, because without either it is incomplete.

outline.heading: Allah has done His part
outline.gist: The Book is His communication and the resurrection is the meeting; what remains is our side.

outline.heading: If We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance
outline.gist: The criminals bow their heads in shame and ask to be sent back now that they have seen.

outline.heading: Who the criminals are
outline.gist: In religious terms the mujrim is the one who does not follow Allah's command or path.

outline.heading: A forced relationship is no relationship
outline.gist: Allah could compel guidance but left the choice to us; we bear the consequence if we do not build it.

outline.heading: Those who fall prostrate when reminded
outline.gist: Prostration is both physical and an inner humility, and they glorify their Lord without arrogance.

outline.heading: Their sides forsake their beds
outline.gist: They are too eager to sleep, calling their Lord in fear and hope and spending from what He provided.

outline.heading: Sajdah as the symbol of brokenness before Allah
outline.gist: Falling prostrate can be the act itself or the heart breaking and submitting; both meanings hold.

outline.heading: Prostration and arrogance cannot share a heart
outline.gist: A heart broken before Allah cannot look down on His creation; it is humble with people.

outline.heading: A unique phrase: like a child too excited to sit
outline.gist: Whenever one side settles the other wants to rise, out of longing to stand before Allah at night.

outline.heading: Living His law beyond the prayer mat
outline.gist: They give zakat and apply His law outside the mihrab; that is a relationship fed by longing, not a boring routine.

outline.heading: Is the believer like the defiantly disobedient?
outline.gist: He recites the comparison and the verse on tasting the lesser punishment before the greater.

outline.heading: Not equal: one who speaks to Allah daily
outline.gist: The one who stands, prostrates and humbles his heart is not like the one who turned his back.

outline.heading: Walking in to a manager you know
outline.gist: Those who knew Allah arrive like a beloved meeting the beloved, like a traveller returning to family.

outline.heading: The runaway slave
outline.gist: Whoever had no relationship with Allah comes like a slave who fled his master; he believes this verse is why we read the surah each week.

outline.heading: The lesser punishment calls us back
outline.gist: Worldly problems, tests, illness and fatigue are placed before the one who turned away so that he wakes up and returns.

outline.heading: Adam running in shame: no refuge from Allah except to Him
outline.gist: Asked if he was fleeing, Adam said it was out of shyness; we have nowhere to go but to Allah.

outline.heading: When is this victory, if you are truthful?
outline.gist: On the day of victory the disbelievers' faith will not help them; turn away and wait.

outline.heading: Musa given the Book; mockers of the day of victory
outline.gist: Those who mock that day gain nothing from believing then.

outline.heading: Who loses when the relationship is refused
outline.gist: Allah loses nothing; the one who refuses to pray and draw near, after Allah offered to hear and answer him, is the loser.

outline.heading: Outro

CuNRWmz5FGg.speaker: adnan
CuNRWmz5FGg.speaker_note: Surah Summaries series at MWN, his cluster framing and voice throughout
CuNRWmz5FGg.title: Surat Al-Ma'arij Summary
CuNRWmz5FGg.one_line: Al-Ma'arij completes the Juz 29 dawah toolkit with behaviour: content perseverance, the eight traits of those who pray, and leaving others' fate to Allah.
CuNRWmz5FGg.summary: He presents Al-Ma'arij as the fourth surah in the Juz 29 cluster on what a caller to Allah needs: after knowledge, ethics and spiritual connection comes behaviour. The title, the ascending ways, recalls that deeds must climb through the heavens to reach Allah and many things can stop them. The command to beautiful patience means persevering without resentment, like Yaqub, content that Allah sends what is best, rather than enduring while hating every moment. Believers see the Day as near because they prepare for it, and anything that ends is short. On that Day loved ones avoid each other's eyes and the guilty would ransom everyone on earth. Human nature is anxious, despairing in hardship and stingy in ease, and must be changed; the exception is those who pray, described through eight traits that begin and end with prayer and are mostly behaviour: giving the needy their right, belief, fear of punishment, chastity, keeping trusts, upright testimony. Knowledge, ethics, connection and behaviour come as one package. Those who claimed Paradise through good family are told Allah alone defines who is good. He then strongly rebukes Muslims' fixation on who will enter Paradise or Hell: do dawah, worry about yourself, and leave judgment to Allah.

outline.heading: The Juz 29 cluster on dawah
outline.gist: These surahs teach what a Muslim needs to carry dawah with his life: knowledge, values, examples, methods and the means to keep going.

outline.heading: Recap: knowledge, ethics and connection
outline.gist: The first three surahs covered how much knowledge, which values and what spiritual connection are needed, without which the message dies off.

outline.heading: Al-Ma'arij: behaviour and the ascending ways
outline.gist: The fourth need is behaviour; the ascending ways recall the Prophet's ascension and the idea that deeds climb through the heavens and can be stopped on the way.

outline.heading: The inevitable punishment and the day of fifty thousand years
outline.gist: Someone asks about a punishment none can hold back; angels and the Spirit ascend to Allah on a day lasting fifty thousand years.

outline.heading: Beautiful patience: perseverance without a grudge
outline.gist: Sabr jamil is perseverance without resentment or self-loathing, as Yaqub said, content with what Allah sends.

outline.heading: Two ways to climb the mountain
outline.gist: Sabr implies real difficulty; one can keep going while hating it or keep going with acceptance and trust that Allah sends the best, and only the second is the beautiful kind.

outline.heading: They see it far, we see it near
outline.gist: Believers see the Day as close because they prepare for it; anything that ends is short, as people in their nineties say of their lives.

outline.heading: Molten sky, woollen mountains, friends who look away
outline.gist: On that Day close friends see each other and avoid eye contact, each too anxious about his own state to ask.

outline.heading: The criminal would ransom everyone on earth
outline.gist: He would offer children, spouse, brother, tribe and all people to escape; the Fire calls those who turned away and hoarded wealth without zakat.

outline.heading: Interlude
Human nature: anxious, despairing, stingy
outline.gist: The soul reacts to extremes, losing hope in hardship and hoarding in ease; these instincts have to change.

outline.heading: Except those who pray: eight traits
outline.gist: Allah does not stop at a generic 'those who pray' but lists eight traits, mostly behaviours with some creed among them.

outline.heading: Constant prayer, the right of the needy, belief and fear
outline.gist: They never neglect prayer, give the deprived a known share of their wealth, believe in the Last Day and never feel secure from Allah's punishment.

outline.heading: Chastity, trusts, covenants and upright testimony
outline.gist: They guard chastity, honour trusts and agreements, and stand by the truth when called to testify without fear or lies.

outline.heading: Wrapped in prayer: the deen comes as a package
outline.gist: The list begins and ends with prayer with behaviours in between; knowledge, ethics, love, fear and behaviour cannot be separated, and disconnecting them ruins how the deen works.

outline.heading: 'We come from good families': Allah defines who is good
outline.gist: Those who wanted Paradise without following were told that being a good person by one's own definition is arrogance; only Allah defines good.

outline.heading: Leave them to play until their Day
outline.gist: Allah could replace them, but this is their chance; they will rush from their graves humbled as if to their idols.

outline.heading: The Prophet: who enters Paradise is not my decision
outline.gist: When people urged him to promise everyone Paradise, he said he only conveys the beliefs, ethics and behaviours Allah requires.

outline.heading: Stop the fixation on who goes to Paradise
outline.gist: Muslims' hundred-year obsession with others' destination is rude to Allah, as if He lacked knowledge, justice or mercy; offer dawah and leave the rest.

outline.heading: The only person you must worry about is you
outline.gist: Dawah is part of your own path to Paradise; tell people what Allah said, behave well yourself, and do not judge or even inquire about their fate.

outline.heading: Interlude
Outro
